definition_zh: 决定性地；无可辩驳地；确凿无疑地
definition_en: in a way that settles a question or proves something so strongly that no doubt remains
core_image: 一只手掌按下盒盖，接缝彻底合拢
scene: In the courtroom, the DNA report conclusively showed that the defendant had not been at the scene.
sceneCN: 这里 conclusively 是「确凿无疑地」（第 2 个义项：以确凿证据证明）；句意：法庭上，DNA 报告确凿无疑地表明被告当时不在现场。图中可辨识物件：法庭、DNA 检测报告、被告席、法官、证物袋。

pos.zh: 决定性地；无可辩驳地；确凿无疑地

senses.title: Settling the matter beyond dispute
senses.titleCN: 决定性地：让争议无从继续
senses.definition: in a manner that ends doubt or argument about a question
senses.definitionCN: 以结束疑问或争论的方式
senses.example: The review conclusively settled the question of who had approved the payment.
senses.exampleCN: 这次复核决定性地弄清了是谁批准了这笔付款。
senses.why: claudere means 'to close'. The -ive suffix gives the adjective the quality of closing, and -ly turns that quality into the manner of an action. To act conclusively is to act in a way that shuts the question.
senses.whyCN: claudere 意为“关闭”。-ive 让形容词带上“关闭”的性质，-ly 再把这种性质变成动作的方式。所谓 conclusively 地行动，就是以把问题合上的方式行动。

senses.title: Proving by hard evidence
senses.titleCN: 确凿证明地：用证据封口
senses.definition: by evidence strong enough to remove every reasonable doubt
senses.definitionCN: 以足以排除一切合理怀疑的证据
senses.example: Tests conclusively proved that the river water contained harmful bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 检测确凿地证明河水里含有有害细菌。
senses.why: The base image is a container with openings. Evidence fills each opening until nothing more can get in, and -ly names the strength with which the case is sealed.
senses.whyCN: 基础意象是一个有开口的容器。证据把每个开口都填满，直到再没有任何东西能进入；-ly 说明的就是封口的力量。

senses.title: Closing a debate
senses.titleCN: 终结争论地：把对话关上
senses.definition: in a way that brings an argument or discussion to an end
senses.definitionCN: 以使争论或讨论结束的方式
senses.example: Her last piece of evidence conclusively ended the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 她最后的证据终结了这场争论。
senses.why: An argument is treated as a space that stays open while people keep talking. Closing it ends the exchange, so the adverb names the manner of that closing.
senses.whyCN: 争论被看成一个只要人还在说就一直敞开的空间。把它关上就结束了交流，副词描述的正是这种关上的方式。

senses.title: Clearly and without ambiguity
senses.titleCN: 明确无疑地：没有第二种读法
senses.definition: in a clear way that cannot reasonably be interpreted differently
senses.definitionCN: 以清楚、不会被合理作他解的方式
senses.example: The data conclusively show a steady decline in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 数据明确无疑地显示出销量的持续下滑。
senses.why: A closed surface has no ambiguous opening. The adverb extends the 'no gap' image from containers to meaning: the statement is shut against a second reading.
senses.whyCN: 合拢的表面没有暧昧的开口。副词把这个“不留缝”的意象从容器扩展到意义：这句话对第二种读法是封闭的。

senses.title: A final legal determination
senses.titleCN: 最终判定地：法律上的定案
senses.definition: as a final and official determination by a court or authority
senses.definitionCN: 作为法院或主管机关的最终正式判定
senses.example: The court conclusively determined where the property line lay.
senses.exampleCN: 法院最终判定确定了地界线的位置。
senses.why: Legal language borrows the same seal: a ruling is 'final' when the matter is closed. The -ly adverb marks the official manner in which the record is shut.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言借用了同一个“封印”：当事情被关上，裁决就是“终局”的。-ly 副词标明的正是案卷被合上的官方方式。

senses.title: Showing by conclusion
senses.titleCN: 结论性地展示：把终点摆出来
senses.definition: in a presentational way that displays a chain of reasoning up to its end
senses.definitionCN: 以展示推理链条直至终点的呈现方式
senses.example: The chart conclusively displays the order in which the events occurred.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图表结论性地展示了事件发生的顺序。
senses.why: The sense is presentational: to show conclusively is to lay out the chain so that its end is visibly shut, with no missing link.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项偏重“呈现”：conclusively 地展示，就是把链条铺开，让它的末端 visibly 合上，中间没有缺环。

senses.title: Ruling out alternatives
senses.titleCN: 决定性地排除：逐扇关门
senses.definition: so completely as to eliminate all other possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底到排除其他一切可能性的方式
senses.example: The fingerprints conclusively ruled out the first suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹决定性地排除了第一名嫌疑人。
senses.why: Exclusion works like shutting doors: each alternative is closed off. The adverb describes the completeness of that closing, leaving one possibility standing.
senses.whyCN: 排除就像逐扇关门：每个替代可能都被关上。副词描述的是这种关闭的彻底程度，最后只留下一种可能。

senses.title: Establishing firmly
senses.titleCN: 决定性地确立：钉牢不留松动
senses.definition: in a way that fixes a fact, link, or principle firmly and permanently
senses.definitionCN: 以牢固而永久地固定事实、联系或原则的方式
senses.example: The experiment conclusively established a link between the two variables.
senses.exampleCN: 这项实验决定性地确立了两个变量之间的联系。
senses.why: To establish is to fix something in place. Conclusively adds that the fixing is sealed, so later argument cannot loosen it.
senses.whyCN: establish 是把某物固定在位置上。conclusively 追加的是“封住”这层意思，使后来的论证无法把它撬松。

senses.title: In the manner of a last word
senses.titleCN: 以最后结论的方式：说完再无可答
senses.definition: as a closing statement that leaves nothing further to be said
senses.definitionCN: 作为不再给人留下回应空间的收尾陈述
senses.example: He spoke conclusively, and nobody in the room raised another objection.
senses.exampleCN: 他以最后结论的口吻说话，房间里没有人再提出异议。
senses.why: This is the social side of claudere: the speaker closes the conversation. The -ly suffix marks the manner of speaking that leaves nothing to answer.
senses.whyCN: 这是 claudere 的社会性一面：说话者把对话关上。-ly 后缀标明的正是那种不给人留回答余地的说话方式。

intro.en: Conclusively is a transparent modern derivative: the Latin verb concludere supplies the meaning, -ive turns it into an adjective, and -ly turns that adjective into an adverb. Dates for the English stages are approximate.
intro.cn: conclusively 是一个结构透明的现代派生词：拉丁动词 concludere 提供意义，-ive 把它变成形容词，-ly 再把形容词变成副词。各英语阶段的年代为大致估计。

items.en: concludere meant 'to shut up, enclose, bring to an end'. Its two parts are con- 'together' and claudere 'to close'; the literal picture is a space shut on every side.
items.cn: concludere 意为“关闭、围合、使结束”。两部分是 con-“一起”和 claudere“关闭”；字面画面是一个四面都合上的空间。

items.en: The past participle conclusus supplied the stem conclus-, which English uses in conclusion, conclusive and conclusively. The stem carries the result 'already shut', not the act of shutting.
items.cn: 过去分词 conclusus 提供了词干 conclus-，英语在 conclusion、conclusive、conclusively 中使用它。这个词干携带的是“已经关上”的结果，而不是关闭的动作。

items.en: conclusive adds -ive, from Latin -ivus, meaning 'having the nature of'. An argument that is conclusive has the nature of a closing: it shuts the case.
items.cn: conclusive 加上 -ive（来自拉丁 -ivus），意为“具有……性质的”。一个 conclusive 的论证具有“关闭”的性质：它把案子合上。

items.en: The move from 'closing' to 'decisive' is metaphorical. Once the last gap is shut, nothing can enter to reopen the question, so 'closed' becomes 'beyond dispute'.
items.cn: 从“关闭”到“决定性”的转变是隐喻性的。最后的缝隙一旦合上，就没有东西能进入重新打开问题，于是“已关闭”变成“无可争辩”。

items.en: conclusive + -ly, from Old English -lice, makes an adverb of manner. It answers 'how' rather than 'what': the proof closes the matter in a conclusive way.
items.cn: conclusive + -ly（来自古英语 -lice）构成方式副词。它回答的是“怎样”，而不是“什么”：这项证明以 conclusive 的方式把事情合上。

items.en: Modern usage is strongest in law and science, where conclusively prove, demonstrate or rule out marks evidence that leaves no room for doubt. The exact first recorded date of the adverb is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代用法最集中于法律和科学语境，conclusively prove、demonstrate 或 rule out 标记的是不留怀疑空间的证据。该副词最早的确切记录年代存疑。

note.en: The first group contains spelling neighbours built on the same Latin verb; the second contains words that come close in meaning but differ in what they emphasize.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一拉丁动词上的形近词；第二组是意思接近、但强调点不同的词。

entries.definition: Stating a conclusion without giving evidence; in law, a conclusory statement is a bare assertion. The -ory suffix marks a tendency or result, not proof.
entries.definitionCN: 只下结论而不给证据的；在法律上，conclusory statement 是未经论证的断言。-ory 后缀标记倾向或结果，并不表示证明。

entries.definition: Including everything or everyone. It comes from includere, in- 'in' + claudere 'close', a cousin of concludere.
entries.definitionCN: 包含一切的；包括所有相关人或物的。它来自 includere（in-“向内”+ claudere“关闭”），是 concludere 的同族词。

entries.definition: Excluding others; restricted to a particular group. From excludere, ex- 'out' + claudere 'close'.
entries.definitionCN: 排他的；仅限于特定群体的。来自 excludere（ex-“向外”+ claudere“关闭”）。

entries.definition: in a way that is final and cannot be changed; it stresses official finality more than evidential force.
entries.definitionCN: 以最终、不可更改的方式；它强调官方意义上的终局性，而非证据力度。

entries.definition: in a way that decides an outcome or contest; it points to the effect on a result rather than to proof.
entries.definitionCN: 以决定结果或胜负的方式；它指向对结局的影响，而不是对证据的证明。

entries.definition: without any doubt; it comments on certainty, not necessarily on the strength of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无疑问地；它评论的是确定性，未必是证据的强度。

entries.definition: in a way that persuades people; it concerns the audience's acceptance, while conclusively concerns the state of the question.
entries.definitionCN: 以令人信服的方式；它关注听众是否接受，而 conclusively 关注问题本身是否已被关上。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be disputed; closest to conclusively, but more often used of facts than of proofs.
entries.definitionCN: 以无可争议的方式；与 conclusively 最接近，但更多用于事实本身，而非证明过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' + claudere 'close': the debater closes the folder and the case together.
normal.cn: con-“一起”+ claudere“关闭”：辩论者把文件夹和案子一起合上。

normal.en: conclusive is an adjective of quality; conclusively is that quality turned into the manner of an action by -ly.
normal.cn: conclusive 是表性质的形容词；conclusively 是 -ly 把这种性质变成动作方式。

normal.en: The standard pairings are conclusively prove, demonstrate and rule out; these show where the word actually lives.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 conclusively prove、demonstrate、rule out；这些搭配显示这个词实际活跃在哪里。

normal.en: conclude, conclusion, conclusive and conclusively all share the same 'shut' stem, so the family reinforces itself.
normal.cn: conclude、conclusion、conclusive、conclusively 都共享同一个“关闭”词干，这个词族彼此强化。

normal.en: inconclusive is the door that will not close: the evidence leaves the question open, and the negative prefix marks that.
normal.cn: inconclusive 是关不上的门：证据让问题继续敞开，否定前缀标记的就是这一点。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy lid pressed down on a box until the seam disappears: that is conclusively.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的盖子压住箱子，直到接缝消失：这就是 conclusively。

abstract.en: Think of the last puzzle piece clicking into place; nothing is missing, so nothing can be added.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一块拼图咔哒落位；什么都不缺，因此也加不进任何东西。

abstract.en: Think of a wax seal stamped on an envelope: the message is closed, and reopening it would break the seal.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上压下一枚火漆印：消息被封住，再打开就会破坏封印。

examples.en: The second experiment conclusively proved that the material conducts electricity.
examples.cn: 第二次实验确凿地证明这种材料能导电。

examples.en: The committee conclusively rejected the proposal after reviewing all the evidence.
examples.cn: 委员会在审阅全部证据后决定性地否决了这项提案。

examples.en: He argued conclusively, leaving his opponent without a reply.
examples.cn: 他的论证无懈可击，让对手无言以对。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯cluding利”——肯（con）把结论（cluding）关进抽屉，利落锁上 → conclusively 决定性地、无可辩驳地

root: 拉丁 concludere“关闭、围合、得出结论”（con-“一起”+ claudere“关闭”）；conclus- 词干 + -ive“有……性质的”+ -ly 副词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one closing gesture: something is shut, and the shutting removes the possibility of another answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个“合拢”动作：某物被关上，而这一关就取消了另一个答案存在的可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lid closing until no gap remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖子合拢，直到不留缝隙。

branches.en: CLOSING AND CLARITY: a closed matter and a closed meaning both leave no opening for another reading.
branches.cn: 合拢与清晰：事情合上、意义合上，两者都不给第二种读法留开口。

branches.en: SEALING WITH EVIDENCE: proof fills every gap, and displaying that proof makes the closure visible.
branches.cn: 用证据封口：证据填满每个缝隙，而把证据展示出来则让合拢过程可见。

branches.en: ENDING THE EXCHANGE: closing a debate and speaking the last word are the social form of the same lid.
branches.cn: 结束交流：终结辩论和说最后一句话，是同一只盖子在社会层面的形态。

branches.en: LEGAL FINALITY AND EXCLUSION: a final ruling shuts the case; ruling out shuts each alternative door.
branches.cn: 法律终局与排除：终局裁决关上案卷；排除则逐扇关上替代选项的门。

branches.en: FIRM ESTABLISHMENT: what is established conclusively is fixed as if sealed in place.
branches.cn: 牢固确立：被 conclusively 确立的东西，像被封印固定住一样。

intro.en: Conclusively is built from live English suffixes on a Latin stem: conclusive + -ly. Only -ive and -ly are productive here; con- and claudere are fossilized inside the base.
intro.cn: conclusively 是在拉丁词干上叠加活的英语后缀：conclusive + -ly。这里只有 -ive 和 -ly 有能产性；con- 与 claudere 已凝固在词基内部。

latinIntro.en: Latin claudere 'to close' is the source of a large family: clause, close, closet, closure, include, exclude, conclude. English borrowed the stems at different times, so the root appears as claud-, claus- or clus-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 claudere“关闭”是一个大词族的源头：clause、close、closet、closure、include、exclude、conclude。英语在不同时期借入这些词干，因此词根会以 claud-、claus- 或 clus- 的形式出现。

items.structure: conclus- (stem of concludere) + -ive (having the nature of)
items.meaning: decisive; putting an end to doubt
items.meaningCN: 决定性的；确凿的（-ive 表示“具有……性质”）
items.example: The evidence was conclusive, and the jury reached a verdict in an hour.
items.exampleCN: 证据是决定性的，陪审团一小时内就作出了裁决。

items.meaning: not leading to a clear decision
items.meaningCN: 非决定性的；无定论的（in-“不”+ conclusive）
items.example: The first test was inconclusive, so they ran a second one.
items.exampleCN: 第一次检测没有定论，于是他们又做了一次。

items.meaning: a judgment reached at the end of reasoning
items.meaningCN: 结论；推论的结果（-ion 构成结果或行为名词）
items.example: The report reaches a clear conclusion about the cause of the fire.
items.exampleCN: 报告对火灾原因得出了明确结论。

items.meaning: to bring to an end; to reach a judgment
items.meaningCN: 结束；得出结论（con-“一起”+ claudere“关闭”）
items.example: The investigators concluded that the accident was caused by human error.
items.exampleCN: 调查人员得出结论，事故由人为失误造成。

items.meaning: in a decisive, doubt-removing way
items.meaningCN: 决定性地；确凿无疑地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The second trial conclusively proved the link.
items.exampleCN: 第二次试验确凿地证明了这一联系。

items.meaning: the quality of being decisive
items.meaningCN: 决定性；确凿性（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The conclusiveness of the evidence surprised even the defence.
items.exampleCN: 证据的决定性连辩方都感到意外。

items.meaning: the act of closing, or a sense of resolution
items.meaningCN: 关闭；了结（-ure 构成结果名词）
items.example: The family finally found closure after the case was solved.
items.exampleCN: 案件告破后，这家人终于得到了心理上的了结。

items.meaning: the act of shutting something out
items.meaningCN: 排除；排斥（ex-“向外”+ clus-“关闭”+ -ion）
items.example: The exclusion of contaminated samples changed the result.
items.exampleCN: 排除受污染的样本改变了结果。

items.meaning: the act of shutting something in; the state of being included
items.meaningCN: 包含；纳入（in-“向内”+ clus-“关闭”+ -ion）
items.example: The inclusion of older data made the trend clearer.
items.exampleCN: 纳入更早的数据让趋势更清楚。

definition_zh: 有条件的；附带条件的；条件性的
definition_en: depending on something else happening or being true; not absolute or unconditional
core_image: 一把只有插对钥匙才转得动的锁
scene: The offer letter stated that admission was conditional on a final transcript and a passing English score.
sceneCN: 这里 conditional 是「有条件的」（第 6 个义项：有条件录取）；句意：录取通知书说明，入学资格以最终成绩单和英语达标成绩为条件。图中可辨识物件：录取通知书、成绩单、英语成绩单、印章、信封。

pos.zh: 有条件的；附条件的；（语法）条件的
条件句；条件式（语法术语）

collocations.zh: 有条件录取；有条件报价

derivatives.zh: 有条件制约的；条件化的

senses.title: Depending on a stated condition
senses.titleCN: 有条件的：以某条件为转移
senses.definition: existing or happening only if something else is true or is done
senses.definitionCN: 只有在另一件事成立或做到时才存在或发生
senses.example: The loan is conditional on a steady income.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款以稳定收入为条件。
senses.why: condicio means an agreed term, and -al means 'pertaining to'. Conditional therefore means 'of the nature of a term': it holds only while the term is met.
senses.whyCN: condicio 意为“商定的条款”，-al 意为“与……有关的”。conditional 因此是“具有条款性质的”：只有条款被满足时它才成立。

senses.title: A conditional agreement
senses.titleCN: 附条件的协议：条款先行
senses.definition: a contract or deal whose force depends on a stated event or requirement
senses.definitionCN: 效力取决于某一约定事件或要求的合同或交易
senses.example: They signed a conditional agreement to buy the warehouse, subject to an inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 他们签了一份附条件的仓库购买协议，须经检验合格。
senses.why: The adjective is applied to the agreement itself. Because the deal carries a term inside it, its force is conditional rather than immediate.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接修饰协议本身。由于交易内部携带一项条款，它的效力是有条件的，而不是立即生效的。

senses.title: The conditional clause in grammar
senses.titleCN: 条件从句：语法中的条件句
senses.definition: a subordinate clause that expresses a condition, typically introduced by if or unless
senses.definitionCN: 表达条件的从句，通常由 if 或 unless 引导
senses.example: In 'If you heat ice, it melts', the if-clause is conditional.
senses.exampleCN: 在 If you heat ice, it melts 中，if 从句是条件从句。
senses.why: Grammar names a clause by its function, and -al marks the class: the clause states a condition on which the main clause depends.
senses.whyCN: 语法按功能给从句命名，-al 标记类别：这个从句陈述主句所依赖的条件。

senses.title: Conditional probability
senses.titleCN: 条件概率：已知某事发生后的概率
senses.definition: the probability of an event given that another event has already occurred
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事件已经发生的条件下，某一事件发生的概率
senses.example: The conditional probability of flooding, given three days of rain, is high.
senses.exampleCN: 在连续降雨三天的条件下，发生洪水的条件概率很高。
senses.why: Statistics borrows the everyday adjective and narrows it: the probability is conditional because its value is tied to the stated event.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用了日常形容词并缩小其范围：这个概率是“有条件的”，因为它的数值绑定在所述事件上。

senses.title: Conditional release in law
senses.titleCN: 有条件释放：带约束的出狱
senses.definition: release from prison or an obligation subject to stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在遵守规定条件的前提下从监狱或义务中获释
senses.example: The board granted him conditional release after eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在十八个月后批准他有条件释放。
senses.why: Law applies -al to release: the release is real, but it exists only while the stated terms hold, so the adjective marks its dependence.
senses.whyCN: 法律把 -al 加在 release 上：释放是真实的，但它只在规定条款持续有效时存在，形容词标记的正是这种依赖关系。

senses.title: Conditional admission or offer
senses.titleCN: 有条件录取/报价：先达标再转正
senses.definition: acceptance or a bid that becomes final only when stated requirements are met
senses.definitionCN: 只有在规定要求满足后才转为最终的录取或报价
senses.example: She accepted a conditional offer that required a score of 90 on the language test.
senses.exampleCN: 她接受了有条件录取，条件是语言考试达到 90 分。
senses.why: Admissions and sales use the same pattern: acceptance is genuine but not final, because a condition stands between the offer and the finished place.
senses.whyCN: 招生和销售使用同一模式：录取是真实的，但不是最终的，因为报价与最终名额之间还立着一项条件。

senses.title: Conditional formatting
senses.titleCN: 条件格式：规则触发样式
senses.definition: in computing, formatting that is applied automatically when a specified rule is met
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机中，当指定规则满足时自动应用的格式
senses.example: Conditional formatting highlights any cell whose value is below zero.
senses.exampleCN: 条件格式会高亮任何数值低于零的单元格。
senses.why: Computing applies -al literally: the formatting is 'pertaining to a condition' that the software tests before changing the display.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域按字面使用 -al：这种格式“与一个条件有关”，软件先检测该条件，再改变显示。

senses.title: Conditional approval
senses.titleCN: 有条件批准：许可附带前提
senses.definition: official consent that remains valid only while specified conditions are satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 只有在规定条件持续满足时才有效的官方同意
senses.example: The agency gave the plant conditional approval while it installed new filters.
senses.exampleCN: 在工厂安装新过滤器的期间，主管机构给予了有条件批准。
senses.why: Approval is official but limited. The -al suffix signals that consent depends on continuing compliance, not on a single signature.
senses.whyCN: 批准是官方的，但有限度。-al 后缀表明这项同意依赖于持续合规，而不是一次签字。

senses.title: The conditional as a noun
senses.titleCN: 名词“条件句/条件式”
senses.definition: in grammar, the conditional mood or a clause of that type, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 语法中的条件式或该类从句，此处作名词使用
senses.example: Spanish uses the conditional to describe what would happen.
senses.exampleCN: 西班牙语用条件式来描述将会发生什么。
senses.why: This is a zero conversion from adjective to noun: the conditional is simply the mood or clause class that the adjective already named.
senses.whyCN: 这是形容词到名词的零派生：the conditional 就是形容词原本所指的那个语气或从句类别。

intro.en: Conditional is not a root word but a derived adjective: English borrowed the noun condition, then attached the Latin suffix -al. The dates below are approximate, and the deeper pre-Latin history of dicere is not traced here.
intro.cn: conditional 不是词根词，而是派生形容词：英语先借入名词 condition，再加拉丁后缀 -al。以下年代为大致估计；dicere 更早的印欧词源在此不作推测。

items.en: condicio(nem) meant 'agreement, stipulation, terms'. It named what two parties had settled, not a physical circumstance.
items.cn: condicio(nem) 意为“协议、约定条款、条件”。它命名的是双方已经谈定的内容，而不是物理环境。

items.en: condicere meant 'to say together, agree upon': con- 'together' plus dicere 'to say'. The terms exist because both sides said the same thing.
items.cn: condicere 意为“共同说定、商定”：con-“一起”加 dicere“说”。条款之所以存在，是因为双方说出了同样的内容。

items.en: English condition came through Old French condition. The stem condition- arrived with the noun, so the suffix could attach directly without a new Latin verb.
items.cn: 英语 condition 经由古法语 condition 传入。词干 condition- 随名词一起进入英语，因此后缀可以直接附着，无需另造拉丁动词。

items.en: -al, from Latin -alis, means 'pertaining to'. Conditional is literally 'pertaining to a condition', hence 'having the nature of a stipulated term'.
items.cn: -al 来自拉丁 -alis，意为“与……有关的”。conditional 字面就是“与条件有关的”，因而表示“具有约定条款性质的”。

items.en: The adjective moves from 'stipulated in an agreement' to 'not absolute'. If performance depends on a term, the thing is conditional rather than unconditional.
items.cn: 这个形容词从“在协议中约定的”转向“非绝对的”。如果履行取决于某项条款，该事物就是有条件的，而不是无条件的。

items.en: Grammar names the conditional clause and mood, statistics names conditional probability, and law and admissions use conditional release and conditional offer. The suffix stays the same; only the field changes.
items.cn: 语法命名条件从句和条件式，统计学命名条件概率，法律与招生使用 conditional release、conditional offer。后缀始终不变，变的只是应用领域。

note.en: The look-alikes below share the condition- stem but add different suffixes; the near-meaning group contains words that also express dependence, each with a different flavour.
note.cn: 下面的形近词共享 condition- 词干，但后缀不同；近义词组也都表达“依赖”，只是各有侧重。

entries.definition: Made dependent on conditions, or trained to respond in a certain way. It is the participle of the verb condition, not a synonym of conditional.
entries.definitionCN: 受条件制约的，或被训练成某种反应的。它是动词 condition 的分词，并不是 conditional 的同义词。

entries.definition: Without any conditions or limits. The un- prefix cancels the conditional link entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 无条件的；没有任何限制的。un- 前缀把“有条件”这一层完全取消。

entries.definition: Something that improves the condition of hair, skin, or air. The -er suffix marks the agent or device, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 改善头发、皮肤或空气状况的产品或装置。-er 后缀标记施动者或器具，而不是性质。

entries.definition: depending on something that may or may not happen. It is common in formal plans, payments, and legal arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 取决于某件未必发生之事的。常用于正式计划、付款和法律安排，比 conditional 更书面。

entries.definition: arranged for the present but likely to be changed. It stresses temporary status rather than stated terms.
entries.definitionCN: 暂定的；目前安排但很可能更改的。它强调临时状态，而非明文条款。

entries.definition: limited or modified by stated exceptions. It is common in approvals, support, and statements.
entries.definitionCN: 受明文例外限制或修正的。常用于批准、支持和陈述。

entries.definition: relying on something else for existence or success. It is the broad everyday word, less technical than conditional.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖另一事物才能存在或成功的。它是宽泛的日常词，技术性弱于 conditional。

entries.definition: not final or fixed; done without full certainty. It stresses hesitation rather than a formal condition.
entries.definitionCN: 暂定的；不确定的；没有十足把握的。它强调犹豫，而不是正式条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real suffix and the real phrases in which the word appears.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的后缀，以及这个词真实出现的短语。

normal.en: condition + -al: the adjective simply says 'having to do with a condition'.
normal.cn: condition + -al：这个形容词只是说“与条件有关”。

normal.en: The key pattern is conditional on: X exists only if Y happens.
normal.cn: 关键句式是 conditional on：X 只有在 Y 发生时才存在。

normal.en: A conditional offer is a real offer with a gate in front of it.
normal.cn: conditional offer 是真实存在的录取或报价，只是前面有一道门槛。

normal.en: Conditional probability is probability with a given fact attached: P(A given B).
normal.cn: 条件概率是附带已知事实的概率：P(A | B)。

normal.en: unconditional is the clean opposite, and the un- makes the contrast visible.
normal.cn: unconditional 是干净的对立项，un- 让这种对比一目了然。

abstract.en: Picture two locks in a row: the door opens only when both keys turn, so the first key alone is conditional.
abstract.cn: 想象一排两把锁：两把钥匙都转动门才开，因此只有第一把钥匙时，一切都是有条件的。

abstract.en: Picture a door held by a chain: it opens only as far as the chain allows.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇被链条拴住的门：它只能开到链条允许的程度。

abstract.en: Picture a contract with a blank line: it is signed, but not complete until the blank is filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同留着一行空白：已经签字，但在空白填上之前并不完整。

examples.en: The sale is conditional on the buyer obtaining a mortgage within thirty days.
examples.cn: 这笔交易以买方在三十天内获得房贷为条件。

examples.en: In the sentence 'If it rains, we will stay home', the first clause is conditional.
examples.cn: 在句子 If it rains, we will stay home 中，第一个从句是条件从句。

examples.en: The software flags overdue tasks through conditional formatting.
examples.cn: 该软件通过条件格式标出逾期任务。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯迪神诺”——肯（con）迪（di）神（tion）诺（al）先把条件讲定才答应 → conditional 有条件的

root: 拉丁 condicio(nem)“约定、条件”，来自 condicere“共同说定”（con-“一起”+ dicere“说”）；condition + -al“与……有关的”。

sensesIntro.en: All nine senses are the same structure at different scales: a main clause, offer, ruling, or setting stands only because a condition stands under it.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都是同一结构在不同尺度上的表现：主句、录取、裁决或设置之所以成立，是因为下面垫着一项条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lock that turns only when a second key is also in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：只有第二把钥匙也到位时，锁才转得动。

branches.en: CORE DEPENDENCE: an ordinary state or agreement holds only while its stated term holds.
branches.cn: 核心依赖：普通状态或协议只有在明文条款成立时才成立。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the conditional clause and the conditional mood are the same dependence expressed in sentence structure.
branches.cn: 语法：条件从句和条件式，是同一依赖关系在句子结构中的表达。

branches.en: PROBABILITY: a value is conditional when it is calculated against a given event.
branches.cn: 概率：当一个数值是相对于已知事件计算出来时，它就是条件性的。

branches.en: LAW AND APPROVAL: release and consent remain valid only while their conditions are met.
branches.cn: 法律与批准：释放和同意只有在条件持续满足时才有效。

branches.en: ADMISSION AND COMPUTING: an offer waits for a requirement, and a format waits for a rule to be true.
branches.cn: 录取与计算机：录取等待要求达成，格式等待规则为真。

intro.en: Conditional is a borrowed noun plus a Latin adjective suffix. -al is the only live derivational suffix in the word; the rest of the base is inherited as a single stem.
intro.cn: conditional 是借入名词加拉丁形容词后缀。词中唯一有能产性的派生后缀是 -al；词基其余部分作为一个整体词干继承下来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb dicere 'to say' also yields dictate, predict, contradict and verdict. condicere is the member that means 'say together', which is why a condition is first of all something agreed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 dicere“说”还衍生出 dictate、predict、contradict、verdict。condicere 是其中表示“一起说”的成员，这正是 condition 首先指“商定之事”的原因。

items.meaning: depending on a condition; not absolute
items.meaningCN: 有条件的；非绝对的（-al 表示“与……有关的”）
items.example: Admission is conditional on passing the entrance test.
items.exampleCN: 入学以通过入学考试为条件。

items.meaning: in a conditional way
items.meaningCN: 有条件地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The plan was conditionally approved pending a review.
items.exampleCN: 该计划在复核前获得有条件批准。

items.meaning: the state of being conditional
items.meaningCN: 条件性；附条件性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The conditionality of the aid was criticized by several governments.
items.exampleCN: 这项援助的附加条件受到若干政府的批评。

items.meaning: a term or state; to train or make dependent
items.meaningCN: 条件；状况；使适应；训练
items.example: The contract sets out the conditions of payment.
items.exampleCN: 合同列明了付款条件。

items.meaning: made dependent or trained
items.meaningCN: 受条件制约的；条件化的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The response is conditioned by years of practice.
items.exampleCN: 这种反应是多年训练塑造出来的。

items.meaning: without conditions
items.meaningCN: 无条件的（un-“不”+ conditional）
items.example: They demanded an unconditional surrender.
items.exampleCN: 他们要求无条件投降。

items.meaning: in a way that has no conditions
items.meaningCN: 无条件地（un- + conditional + -ly）
items.example: She supported her brother unconditionally.
items.exampleCN: 她无条件地支持弟弟。

items.meaning: a condition that must be met first
items.meaningCN: 先决条件（pre-“在前”+ condition）
items.example: A ceasefire is a precondition for the talks.
items.exampleCN: 停火是谈判的先决条件。

items.meaning: something that improves condition
items.meaningCN: 护发素；调节器（-er 表示施动者或器具）
items.example: Use a conditioner after shampooing to soften the hair.
items.exampleCN: 洗发后使用护发素让头发柔顺。

latinEntries.meaning: to say together, agree on terms

definition_zh: 条件作用；条件反射训练；调理；训练
definition_en: the process of training behaviour through repeated stimuli, or of bringing something into a desired condition
core_image: 反复按同一个按钮，让反应变成不假思索
scene: In the lab, the rat learned to press a lever because every press brought a food pellet, a clear case of operant conditioning.
sceneCN: 这里 conditioning 是「操作性条件作用」（第 2 个义项：通过结果强化塑造行为）；句意：实验室里，老鼠因为每次按杆都会得到食物丸而学会按杆，这是操作性条件作用的典型案例。图中可辨识物件：斯金纳箱、金属杆、食物丸、老鼠、记录曲线。

pos.zh: 条件作用；条件反射训练
调理；训练；调节（多作定语，如 conditioning agent）

forms.label: 复数（罕用，指多种条件作用）
动词 condition 的现在分词

derivatives.zh: 条件化的；受条件制约的

senses.title: Behavioural conditioning by repetition
senses.titleCN: 行为条件反射训练：重复塑形
senses.definition: the process of training a person or animal to respond in a particular way through repeated experience
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复经验把人或动物训练成特定反应的过程
senses.example: Years of conditioning made the dog sit whenever the bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的条件反射训练让这只狗一听到铃声就坐下。
senses.why: condition is the base and -ing makes it a process noun: conditioning is not one act but the repeated bringing of behaviour into a set condition.
senses.whyCN: condition 是词基，-ing 把它变成过程名词：conditioning 不是一次动作，而是把行为反复带入某个既定状态的过程。

senses.title: Operant conditioning: shaping by consequences
senses.titleCN: 操作性条件作用：用结果塑形
senses.definition: learning in which behaviour is shaped by rewards and punishments that follow it
senses.definitionCN: 由行为之后的奖励和惩罚来塑造行为的学习过程
senses.example: Operant conditioning rewarded the rat with food each time it pressed the lever.
senses.exampleCN: 操作性条件作用在老鼠每次按杆时用食物奖励它。
senses.why: Here -ing names the whole training loop: an action, a consequence, and a changed likelihood of repeating the action.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ing 命名的是整个训练回路：一个动作、一个结果，以及该动作再次发生的概率变化。

senses.title: Classical conditioning: pairing stimuli
senses.titleCN: 经典条件作用：把刺激配对
senses.definition: learning in which a neutral stimulus becomes linked to a reflexive response through repeated pairing
senses.definitionCN: 中性刺激通过反复配对而与反射性反应建立联系的学习过程
senses.example: Pavlov's classical conditioning paired a bell with food until the bell alone triggered salivation.
senses.exampleCN: 巴甫洛夫的经典条件作用把铃声与食物配对，直到铃声单独就能引发唾液分泌。
senses.why: The process noun describes pairing rather than reward: two things are repeatedly placed together until one comes to stand for the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程中名词描述的是“配对”而非奖励：两样东西被反复放在一起，直到其中一个能代表另一个。

senses.title: Physical conditioning: building fitness
senses.titleCN: 体能训练：把身体练到状态
senses.definition: exercise that trains the body for strength, endurance, or a particular sport
senses.definitionCN: 为增强力量、耐力或适应某项运动而进行的身体训练
senses.example: The team spent six weeks on physical conditioning before the season.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在赛季前进行了六周体能训练。
senses.why: The older sense of condition is 'to bring into good condition'. With -ing, the word names the ongoing work of putting the body into that state.
senses.whyCN: condition 较早的义项是“使处于良好状态”。加上 -ing，这个词命名的是把身体逐步带入该状态的持续工作。

senses.title: Hair and skin conditioning
senses.titleCN: 头发/皮肤调理：改善表面状态
senses.definition: treatment that makes hair or skin softer, smoother, and easier to manage
senses.definitionCN: 使头发或皮肤更柔软、顺滑、易打理的处理
senses.example: This shampoo includes a conditioning agent that smooths the hair.
senses.exampleCN: 这款洗发水含有一种能让头发顺滑的调理成分。
senses.why: The same process noun is applied to a surface: a conditioner is the agent, and conditioning is the action of bringing hair or skin into a better condition.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过程名词被用于表面：conditioner 是施动产品，conditioning 则是把头发或皮肤带入更好状态的动作。

senses.title: Air conditioning: controlling indoor air
senses.titleCN: 空气调节：控制室内空气状态
senses.definition: the process of controlling the temperature, humidity, and quality of air in a space
senses.definitionCN: 控制某一空间内空气温度、湿度和质量的过程
senses.example: The office air conditioning failed during the hottest week of summer.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的空调在夏天最热的一周坏了。
senses.why: Air conditioning is a fixed phrase in which -ing still means 'bringing into a condition'; the object is simply the air of a room.
senses.whyCN: air conditioning 是固定短语，其中的 -ing 仍表示“使进入某种状态”，只不过作用对象变成房间里的空气。

senses.title: Conditioning as a general process
senses.titleCN: 条件化过程：让事物取决于条件
senses.definition: the general process by which something is made to depend on or conform to conditions
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物依赖或符合条件的一般过程
senses.example: The conditioning of new employees takes place through daily routines.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工的条件化过程通过日常惯例发生。
senses.why: This is the broadest use: the verb condition means 'to attach conditions to', and -ing turns that into the process of attaching or imposing them.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的用法：动词 condition 意为“给……附加条件”，-ing 把它变成附加或施加条件的过程。

senses.title: Social conditioning
senses.titleCN: 社会条件塑造：环境长期训练
senses.definition: the influence of society that shapes a person's beliefs, habits, and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 社会对个人信念、习惯和行为的影响与塑造
senses.example: Social conditioning taught her to apologize for asking questions.
senses.exampleCN: 社会条件塑造让她为提出问题而道歉。
senses.why: Society is treated as the trainer. The -ing process noun extends from laboratory training to the long, repeated shaping done by a culture.
senses.whyCN: 社会被当作训练者。这个 -ing 过程名词从实验室训练扩展到文化长期反复进行的塑造。

senses.title: Adaptation through training
senses.titleCN: 训练适应过程：身体逐步调整
senses.definition: the gradual adjustment of body or mind to repeated physical or mental demands
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心理对反复出现的体力或脑力要求逐步作出的调整
senses.example: Athletic conditioning improves recovery as well as performance.
senses.exampleCN: 运动训练既提高表现，也改善恢复能力。
senses.why: The -ing form highlights gradualness: repeated demands bring the body into condition, and the process continues rather than ending at one session.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式突出渐进性：反复的要求把身体带入状态，而这个过程中持续进行，并不在某一次训练后结束。

intro.en: Conditioning is a derived process noun: the borrowed base condition receives the native -ing suffix. The psychological sense is recent and technical; the older senses are about bringing something into a condition. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conditioning 是派生的过程名词：借入的词基 condition 接受本族语后缀 -ing。心理学义项较晚且属术语；较早的义项都是“把某物带入某种状态”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base is Latin condicio(nem) 'agreement, stipulation', from condicere 'to say together, agree upon'. The earliest meaning is a settled term, not a state of matter.
items.cn: 词基是拉丁 condicio(nem)“协议、约定”，来自 condicere“共同说定”。最早的意思是谈定的条款，而不是物质状态。

items.en: English first used condition as a noun, then as a verb meaning 'to subject to conditions' and later 'to train or accustom'. The verb is the door through which -ing enters.
items.cn: 英语先以 condition 作名词，后来用作动词，表示“使受条件制约”，再发展出“训练、使习惯”。动词是 -ing 进入这个词的入口。

items.en: The native -ing suffix forms nouns of action or process. Attaching it to condition yields 'the process of conditioning', which can name an ongoing activity rather than a single event.
items.cn: 本族语 -ing 后缀构成动作或过程名词。附着在 condition 上就得到“conditioning 的过程”，可命名持续活动而非单次事件。

items.en: In 19c. sport and horse training, conditioning meant bringing the body into condition through regular exercise. The -ing form names the work, not the finished state.
items.cn: 在 19 世纪的运动和马匹训练中，conditioning 指通过规律锻炼把身体带入良好状态。-ing 形式命名的是这项工作，而不是完成后的状态。

items.en: Pavlov's work on paired stimuli and later Skinner's work on consequences made conditioning a technical term. Here -ing names a learning process: classical or operant.
items.cn: 巴甫洛夫关于刺激配对的研究以及后来斯金纳关于结果的研究，使 conditioning 成为术语。这里的 -ing 命名的是学习过程：经典的或操作性的。

items.en: Air conditioning and hair conditioning spread the same process noun into technology and personal care. The core remains 'bringing something into a desired condition'.
items.cn: air conditioning 和 hair conditioning 把同一个过程名词扩展到技术与个人护理。核心仍然是“把某物带入理想状态”。

note.en: The look-alikes are built from the same condition base with other endings. The near-meaning words all describe shaping or training, but differ in mechanism and register.
note.cn: 形近词都由同一个 condition 词基加其他词尾构成。近义词都描述塑造或训练，但在机制和语体上不同。

entries.definition: A term, a state, or the act of training. It is the base from which conditioning is derived, not the process noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 条件、状态，或训练这一动作。它是 conditioning 的词基，而不是过程名词本身。

entries.definition: Already trained or made dependent. It describes the result, while conditioning describes the process.
entries.definitionCN: 已被训练好的或受条件制约的。它描述结果，而 conditioning 描述过程。

entries.definition: A product or device that improves condition, such as hair conditioner or an air conditioner.
entries.definitionCN: 改善状态的产品或装置，如护发素或空调设备。

entries.definition: The general activity of teaching a skill or behaviour through practice. It is broader and less technical than conditioning.
entries.definitionCN: 通过练习教授技能或行为的一般活动。它比 conditioning 更宽泛，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: The gradual weakening of a response after repeated exposure to a stimulus. It reduces a reaction rather than builds one.
entries.definitionCN: 反复接触刺激后反应逐渐减弱。它是在削弱反应，而不是建立反应。

entries.definition: The process by which people learn the norms of a society. It overlaps with social conditioning but stresses norms and learning.
entries.definitionCN: 人们学习社会规范的过程。它与社会条件塑造重叠，但强调规范和习得。

entries.definition: Training or restoring something again after decline or damage. The re- prefix marks repetition or restoration.
entries.definitionCN: 在衰退或损坏之后重新训练或修复。re- 前缀标记重复或恢复。

entries.definition: Repeated mechanical practice. It stresses repetition of an exercise, not the shaping of a response by stimuli.
entries.definitionCN: 反复机械的操练。它强调练习的重复，而不是用刺激塑造反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base verb, the real process suffix, and the real technical phrases that keep the word alive.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词基动词、真实的过程后缀，以及让这个词保持活力的真实术语搭配。

normal.en: condition + -ing: the suffix turns 'bring into a condition' into 'the process of bringing into a condition'.
normal.cn: condition + -ing：后缀把“使进入状态”变成“使进入状态的过程”。

normal.en: Classical and operant are the two main laboratory routes: pairing stimuli versus rewarding consequences.
normal.cn: 经典与操作性是实验室里的两条主要路径：配对刺激，对比奖励结果。

normal.en: Air conditioning is the same process noun applied to air, not a separate word.
normal.cn: air conditioning 是同一个过程名词用在空气上，并不是另一个词。

normal.en: A conditioner is the product; conditioning is the action it performs.
normal.cn: conditioner 是产品；conditioning 是它所执行的动作。

normal.en: Social conditioning is society playing the trainer, repeating its lessons until they feel natural.
normal.cn: 社会条件塑造就是社会扮演训练者，重复它的课程，直到这些课程显得理所当然。

abstract.en: Think of a path worn into grass: no single walk makes it, but repetition turns the route into the obvious one.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上被踏出的一条路：没有哪一次行走能造成它，是反复行走让这条路线变成显而易见的选择。

abstract.en: Think of a thermostat: it does not change the room once, it keeps bringing the room back to a set condition.
abstract.cn: 想象恒温器：它不是只改变房间一次，而是不断把房间带回设定状态。

abstract.en: Think of a bar of soap used again and again on the same spot: the surface slowly becomes smoother.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肥皂反复用在同一个部位：表面慢慢变得更光滑。

examples.en: Classical conditioning explains why the dog salivates at the sound of the bell.
examples.cn: 经典条件作用解释了为什么这只狗一听到铃声就分泌唾液。

examples.en: The coach designed a conditioning programme to build endurance before the finals.
examples.cn: 教练设计了一套体能训练方案，为决赛前建立耐力。

examples.en: Poor air conditioning made the packed train uncomfortable.
examples.cn: 糟糕的空调让拥挤的列车很不舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯迪神宁”——肯（con）迪（di）神（tion）宁（ing）反复训练到条件反射 → conditioning 条件作用、调理

root: condition（拉丁 condicio“约定、条件”）+ -ing（过程名词后缀）；从“反复设定条件”引申为“训练成自动反应”与“调理、调节”。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of conditioning is a process, never a single act: something is repeatedly exposed, exercised, or treated until its state changes.
sensesIntro.cn: conditioning 的每个义项都是过程，而不是单次动作：某物被反复暴露、锻炼或处理，直到它的状态发生改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same button pressed again and again until the response needs no thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个按钮被反复按下，直到反应不再需要思考。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR: repetition, reward, or pairing installs a response that later appears on its own.
branches.cn: 行为：重复、奖励或配对安装出一种反应，之后它会自行出现。

branches.en: THE BODY: exercise repeatedly brings strength and endurance into condition, and adaptation is the gradual result.
branches.cn: 身体：锻炼反复把力量与耐力带入状态，适应则是逐渐产生的结果。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: shampoo and conditioner treat hair or skin until it reaches a better condition.
branches.cn: 表面：洗发与护发处理作用于头发或皮肤，直到达到更好的状态。

branches.en: THE AIR: a room is repeatedly adjusted until temperature and humidity stay at a set condition.
branches.cn: 空气：房间被持续调节，直到温度和湿度维持在设定状态。

branches.en: THE GENERAL AND SOCIAL: conditions are attached to people, and a culture repeats its lessons until they become habits.
branches.cn: 一般与社会：条件被附加到人身上，而文化重复它的课程直到其成为习惯。

intro.en: Conditioning is a native suffix on a borrowed base: condition + -ing. The suffix is fully productive and carries the process meaning; the base supplies the idea of a condition or state.
intro.cn: conditioning 是借入词基加本族语后缀：condition + -ing。后缀完全能产，承担“过程”意义；词基提供“条件、状态”的观念。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind the base is condicio and condicere, from dicere 'to say'. English relatives outside conditioning include condition, conditional, precondition and recondition.
latinIntro.cn: 词基背后的拉丁词族是 condicio 和 condicere，源头为 dicere“说”。conditioning 之外的英语同族词包括 condition、conditional、precondition、recondition。

items.meaning: the process of training or bringing into a state
items.meaningCN: 条件作用；训练或调理的过程（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: Conditioning takes time because it depends on repetition.
items.exampleCN: 条件作用需要时间，因为它依赖重复。

items.meaning: a term or state; to train or make dependent
items.meaningCN: 条件；状态；使适应；训练
items.example: The trainer conditions the horse to accept a saddle.
items.exampleCN: 驯马师训练这匹马接受马鞍。

items.meaning: a product or device that improves condition
items.meaningCN: 护发素；调节器（-er 表示施动者或器具）
items.example: Apply the conditioner and leave it on for two minutes.
items.exampleCN: 涂上护发素，停留两分钟。

items.meaning: trained or made dependent
items.meaningCN: 条件化的；受制约的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The conditioned response appeared as soon as the light flashed.
items.exampleCN: 灯光一闪，条件化反应就出现了。

items.meaning: without conditions
items.meaningCN: 无条件的（un-“不”+ conditional）
items.example: The dog gave its owner unconditional trust.
items.exampleCN: 这只狗无条件地信任主人。

items.meaning: a condition that must be met first
items.meaningCN: 先决条件（pre-“在前”+ condition）
items.example: Good sleep is a precondition for effective training.
items.exampleCN: 良好睡眠是有效训练的先决条件。

items.meaning: to restore or train again
items.meaningCN: 翻新；重新训练（re-“再次”+ condition）
items.example: The workshop reconditions old engines for sale.
items.exampleCN: 这家工坊翻新旧发动机用于出售。

items.meaning: the state of being conditional
items.meaningCN: 条件性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The conditionality of the funding worried the researchers.
items.exampleCN: 资金附带的条件让研究人员担忧。

items.meaning: fitted with air conditioning
items.meaningCN: 装有空调的（air + conditioned 复合形容词）
items.example: The library is air-conditioned throughout the summer.
items.exampleCN: 整个夏天图书馆都开着空调。

latinEntries.meaning: to say together, agree on terms
a saying, a word, a delivery

definition_zh: 导电性；导热性；传导率；电导率
definition_en: the ability of a material to carry electricity or heat, usually measured as the reciprocal of resistivity
core_image: 一条让电流顺畅通过的水管
scene: In the lab, the engineer measured the conductivity of a copper wire and found it far higher than that of a plastic rod.
sceneCN: 这里 conductivity 是「导电性」（第 1 个义项：材料传导电流的能力）；句意：实验室里，工程师测量铜线的导电性，发现它远高于塑料棒。图中可辨识物件：万用表、铜线、塑料棒、电极、读数屏。

pos.zh: 导电性；导热性（不可数，指材料性质）
电导率（可数，指具体测量值）

forms.label: 复数（罕用，指多种材料或多次测量的电导率）

senses.title: Electrical conductivity
senses.titleCN: 导电性：让电流通过的能力
senses.definition: the ability of a material to carry an electric current
senses.definitionCN: 材料传导电流的能力
senses.example: Copper's high electrical conductivity makes it the standard material for wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 铜的高导电性使它成为电线的标准材料。
senses.why: conducere means 'to lead together'. -ive gives the adjective the quality of leading, and -ity names that quality as a measurable state: the capacity to lead current through.
senses.whyCN: conducere 意为“一起引导”。-ive 给形容词“引导”的性质，-ity 再把这种性质命名为可测量的状态：把电流引导过去的能力。

senses.title: Thermal conductivity
senses.titleCN: 导热性：让热量通过的能力
senses.definition: the ability of a material to carry heat through itself
senses.definitionCN: 材料把热量传导通过自身的能力
senses.example: The thermal conductivity of aluminium is lower than that of copper.
senses.exampleCN: 铝的导热性低于铜。
senses.why: The same 'leading through' image is applied to heat rather than charge. The -ity noun stays unchanged; only the carried quantity differs.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“引导通过”的意象被用在热量而非电荷上。-ity 名词本身不变，变的只是被传导的东西。

senses.title: Conductivity of water
senses.titleCN: 水的电导率：溶解离子的读数
senses.definition: a measure of how well water carries current, used to estimate dissolved ions
senses.definitionCN: 衡量水传导电流好坏的指标，用来估计溶解离子的多少
senses.example: The conductivity of the stream rose sharply after the fertilizer runoff.
senses.exampleCN: 化肥径流之后，这条溪水的电导率急剧上升。
senses.why: The abstract quality is now attached to a sample. Pure water conducts little, so the measured -ity value reveals how much dissolved salt is 'leading' the current.
senses.whyCN: 抽象性质此时附着在一个样本上。纯水几乎不导电，因此测得的 -ity 数值能显示有多少溶解盐在“引导”电流。

senses.title: High or low conductivity
senses.titleCN: 高/低导电性：性质有高低之分
senses.definition: the degree to which a material conducts, described on a scale from low to high
senses.definitionCN: 材料传导的程度，可用从低到高的尺度描述
senses.example: Pure water has very low conductivity until salts are added.
senses.exampleCN: 纯水的导电性很低，直到加入盐类才改变。
senses.why: -ity is a quality noun that admits degrees. Because conductivity can be strong or weak, it naturally takes high and low as modifiers.
senses.whyCN: -ity 是允许程度差异的性质名词。导电性可以强也可以弱，因此自然可以受 high、low 修饰。

senses.title: A measured conductivity value
senses.titleCN: 电导率测量：从性质到读数
senses.definition: a conductivity value obtained by measurement and reported in a test result
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量得到、写在检测结果中的电导率数值
senses.example: The lab reports conductivity in microsiemens per centimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室以微西门子每厘米报告电导率。
senses.why: Measurement turns the abstract noun into a count noun: a particular conductivity is the value that the instrument produced.
senses.whyCN: 测量把抽象名词变成可数名词：某一次 conductivity 就是仪器给出的那个具体数值。

senses.title: Ionic conductivity
senses.titleCN: 离子导电性：靠离子搬运电荷
senses.definition: conduction carried by moving ions rather than by free electrons
senses.definitionCN: 由移动的离子而不是自由电子来传导电荷
senses.example: Ionic conductivity in the gel allows the battery to work at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 凝胶中的离子导电性使电池能在室温下工作。
senses.why: Here 'leading through' is done by ions. The compound simply specifies the carriers, while -ity still names the capacity to conduct.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“引导通过”由离子完成。复合词只是指定了载流者，-ity 仍然命名传导能力。

senses.title: A reading from a conductivity meter
senses.titleCN: 电导率仪读数：仪器语境中的简称
senses.definition: the value shown by a conductivity meter, often called simply 'the conductivity' in lab shorthand
senses.definitionCN: 电导率仪显示的值，实验室口语中常直接简称 conductivity
senses.example: Check the conductivity before you add more salts to the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 在往槽里加更多盐之前，先看一下电导率读数。
senses.why: This is metonymy, not a new sense of the suffix: the meter measures the quantity, and speakers shorten 'the conductivity reading' to 'the conductivity'.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻，而不是后缀产生了新义：仪器测量的是这个量，说话者把 the conductivity reading 简称为 the conductivity。

senses.title: A material's conducting performance
senses.titleCN: 材料导电性能：选材时的比较指标
senses.definition: a material property used to compare substances when choosing one for a design
senses.definitionCN: 在选择设计材料时用来比较不同物质的材料属性
senses.example: Designers compare the conductivity of alloys before choosing one for a connector.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师在选择连接器材料前会比较各种合金的导电性能。
senses.why: The -ity noun names an intrinsic property of the material itself, so it can be listed, compared and ranked in engineering tables.
senses.whyCN: 这个 -ity 名词命名的是材料本身的固有属性，因此可以列入工程表格、相互比较并排序。

senses.title: Conductivity as a quantity with units
senses.titleCN: 电导率单位：西门子每米
senses.definition: the physical quantity expressed in siemens per metre in the SI system
senses.definitionCN: 在国际单位制中以西门子每米表示的物理量
senses.example: Conductivity is expressed in siemens per metre in SI units.
senses.exampleCN: 在国际单位制中，电导率用西门子每米表示。
senses.why: Once a property is measured, it becomes a quantity. The -ity noun supplies the name of the quantity, and the unit tells how much of it is present.
senses.whyCN: 一种性质一旦可测量，就成了物理量。-ity 名词提供这个量的名称，单位则说明它有多少。

intro.en: Conductivity is a scientific derivative built in stages: Latin conducere gives the verb, -ive makes an adjective, and -ity makes the abstract noun. The first recorded uses of the full noun are 19c. and should be treated as approximate.
intro.cn: conductivity 是分阶段构造出的科学派生词：拉丁 conducere 提供动词，-ive 构成形容词，-ity 构成抽象名词。完整名词的最早记录在 19 世纪，具体年代应按大致估计看待。

items.en: conducere meant 'to bring together, lead, convey', from con- 'together' and ducere 'to lead'. The root image is a guide moving something along a path.
items.cn: conducere 意为“聚拢、引导、输送”，由 con-“一起”和 ducere“引导”构成。词根意象是一个引导者把某物沿路径带过去。

items.en: English conduct appears in the 15c. with the senses 'to lead, guide' and 'to convey'. The physical sense of conveying electricity or heat developed later.
items.cn: 英语 conduct 在 15 世纪出现，带有“引导、带领”和“输送”的义项。输送电或热的物理义项后来才发展出来。

items.en: conductive adds -ive, from Latin -ivus, 'having the nature of'. A conductive material has the nature of leading charge or heat from one place to another.
items.cn: conductive 加上 -ive（来自拉丁 -ivus），意为“具有……性质的”。导电材料具有把电荷或热量从一处引导到另一处的性质。

items.en: conductive + -ity, from Latin -itas, creates an abstract quality noun. Conductivity is the state or quality of being conductive, coined for scientific measurement rather than everyday talk.
items.cn: conductive + -ity（来自拉丁 -itas）构成抽象性质名词。conductivity 就是“具有传导性”的状态或性质，是为科学测量而非日常谈话创造的词。

items.en: The noun narrowed from general 'leading' to the measurable physical property of carrying electricity or heat. The exact first recorded use is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词从泛泛的“引导”缩小为可测量的物理属性：传导电或热。确切的最早记录存疑。

items.en: Modern science expresses conductivity in siemens per metre and extends it to water quality, ionic transport, and materials selection. The suffix chain stays visible in every use.
items.cn: 现代科学用西门子每米表示电导率，并把它扩展到水质、离子传输和材料选型。每一种用法中都仍能看见这条后缀链。

note.en: The look-alikes share the conduct- stem with different endings; the near-meaning group contains quantities and properties that are often confused in physics.
note.cn: 形近词共享 conduct- 词干但词尾不同；近义词组包含物理学中常被混淆的量与性质。

entries.definition: The process of heat or charge passing through a material. It names the event, while conductivity names the property that allows it.
entries.definitionCN: 热或电荷通过材料的过程。它命名事件，而 conductivity 命名允许该事件发生的性质。

entries.definition: Able to conduct electricity or heat. It is the adjective stage between conduct and conductivity.
entries.definitionCN: 能导电或导热的。它是 conduct 与 conductivity 之间的形容词阶段。

entries.definition: A material or object that conducts, or a person who directs an orchestra. The -or suffix marks the one that conducts.
entries.definitionCN: 导体；导电材料或物体，也指乐队指挥。-or 后缀标记执行传导的东西。

entries.definition: The reciprocal of resistance: how easily a particular object carries current. Conductivity is a property of the material, conductance of the object.
entries.definitionCN: 电阻的倒数：某个特定物体导电的容易程度。conductivity 是材料属性，conductance 是物体属性。

entries.definition: The intrinsic resistance of a material. Conductivity is its reciprocal, so the two describe the same property from opposite directions.
entries.definitionCN: 材料固有的电阻率。conductivity 是它的倒数，两者从相反方向描述同一属性。

entries.definition: Opposition to current in a particular object, measured in ohms. It is the everyday opposite of easy conduction.
entries.definitionCN: 特定物体对电流的阻碍，用欧姆测量。它是“容易传导”的日常对立面。

entries.definition: How readily a material allows a field or fluid to pass through. It is a parallel property, not a measure of charge transport.
entries.definitionCN: 材料允许多少场或流体通过的容易程度。它是并行的属性，不是电荷传输的度量。

entries.definition: The fraction of light or radiation that passes through a sample. It concerns radiation, not electrical current.
entries.definitionCN: 光或辐射透过样本的比例。它涉及辐射，不涉及电流。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the two live suffixes, and the standard laboratory phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、两个活后缀，以及标准的实验室搭配。

normal.en: con- 'together' + ducere 'lead': conductivity is the capacity to lead charge through a material.
normal.cn: con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”：conductivity 就是把电荷引导通过材料的能力。

normal.en: -ive makes 'conductive', and -ity turns that adjective into a measurable property.
normal.cn: -ive 构成 conductive，-ity 再把形容词变成可测量的属性。

normal.en: Copper is the everyday example: high conductivity, which is why wires are made of it.
normal.cn: 铜是日常例子：高导电性，这正是电线用铜的原因。

normal.en: Thermal conductivity is the same noun with heat as the cargo instead of electrons.
normal.cn: thermal conductivity 是同一个名词，只是货物从电子换成了热量。

normal.en: resistivity is the inverse; when one goes up in the data, the other tends to go down.
normal.cn: resistivity 是倒数关系；数据中一个升高时，另一个往往下降。

abstract.en: Think of a wide, smooth pipe: water passes easily, and that ease is conductivity.
abstract.cn: 想象一根又宽又滑的水管：水很容易通过，这种“容易”就是 conductivity。

abstract.en: Think of a toll road with many open lanes: charge moves fast and few obstacles slow it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条开了很多通道的收费公路：电荷移动很快，少有障碍拖慢它。

abstract.en: Think of a relay race: the baton is passed from hand to hand, just as energy is passed from particle to particle.
abstract.cn: 想象接力赛：接力棒从一只手传到另一只手，正如能量从粒子传到粒子。

examples.en: The conductivity of seawater is much higher than that of fresh water because of dissolved salts.
examples.cn: 由于溶解盐分，海水的电导率远高于淡水。

examples.en: Engineers test the thermal conductivity of new insulation before using it in buildings.
examples.cn: 工程师在把新型保温材料用于建筑之前，会测试它的导热性。

examples.en: A conductivity meter showed that the soil sample contained unusually high levels of salt.
examples.cn: 电导率仪显示这份土壤样本的盐分异常高。

dict_mnemonic.text: “康达克提维提”——康（con）达（duc）克（tive）提维提（tivity）让电流像水管一样一路通到底 → conductivity 导电性

root: 拉丁 conducere“一起引导、带领”（con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”）；conduct + -ive“有……性质的”+ -ity“性质、状态”。

sensesIntro.en: All nine senses describe one capacity: something is led through a material. The variation is in what is led (charge, heat, ions) and how that capacity is measured or used.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都描述同一种能力：某物被引导穿过材料。变化在于被引导的是什么（电荷、热、离子），以及这种能力如何被测量或使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe wide enough to let the flow pass without obstruction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根足够宽、让流体无阻通过的水管。

branches.en: ELECTRICAL CAPACITY: a material lets current pass, and the degree can be high or low.
branches.cn: 导电能力：材料让电流通过，程度可分高低。

branches.en: THERMAL CAPACITY: the same leading-through image is applied to heat.
branches.cn: 导热能力：同一个“引导通过”的意象被用在热上。

branches.en: WATER AND MEASUREMENT: dissolved ions make water conductive, and a test turns that property into a reported value.
branches.cn: 水与测量：溶解离子使水导电，检测则把这种性质变成报告数值。

branches.en: IONIC TRANSPORT: the carriers are ions, but the noun still names the capacity to conduct.
branches.cn: 离子传输：载流者是离子，但这个名词仍然命名传导能力。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT, MATERIAL, UNIT: a meter reads it, engineers compare it, and SI units quantify it.
branches.cn: 仪器、材料与单位：仪器读出它，工程师比较它，国际单位制量化它。

intro.en: Conductivity stacks two productive suffixes on a Latin verb stem: conduct + -ive + -ity. -ive builds the adjective and -ity the abstract noun; neither suffix changes its basic function here.
intro.cn: conductivity 在拉丁动词词干上叠加两个能产后缀：conduct + -ive + -ity。-ive 构成形容词，-ity 构成抽象名词；两个后缀在此都没有改变基本功能。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'to lead' is the root of a wide family: conduct, introduce, produce, reduce, deduce, educate. conducere is the member that means 'lead together', which is why conduct first meant 'guide or convey'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”是一个大词族的根：conduct、introduce、produce、reduce、deduce、educate。conducere 是其中表示“一起引导”的成员，这正是 conduct 最初表示“引导、输送”的原因。

items.meaning: the ability to conduct electricity or heat
items.meaningCN: 导电性；导热性；传导率（-ive + -ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The conductivity of the alloy falls as its temperature rises.
items.exampleCN: 这种合金的电导率随温度升高而下降。

items.meaning: able to conduct electricity or heat
items.meaningCN: 导电的；导热的（-ive 表示“具有……性质”）
items.example: The gel is conductive enough to link the two electrodes.
items.exampleCN: 这种凝胶的导电性足以连接两个电极。

items.meaning: the process of carrying heat or charge
items.meaningCN: 传导过程（-ion 构成过程名词）
items.example: Conduction through the rod was slow because the metal was impure.
items.exampleCN: 由于金属不纯，通过这根杆的传导很慢。

items.meaning: a material that conducts, or a person who directs
items.meaningCN: 导体；指挥（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.
items.exampleCN: 铜是良好的电导体。

items.meaning: to carry, convey, or lead; behaviour
items.meaningCN: 传导；实施；行为（con-“一起”+ ducere“引导”）
items.example: The wires conduct the current to the motor.
items.exampleCN: 电线把电流传导到电动机。

items.meaning: a material that conducts only under certain conditions
items.meaningCN: 半导体（semi-“半”+ conductor）
items.example: Silicon is the most common semiconductor in electronics.
items.exampleCN: 硅是电子设备中最常见的半导体。

items.meaning: zero electrical resistance below a critical temperature
items.meaningCN: 超导性（super-“超过”+ conductivity）
items.example: Superconductivity allows current to flow without loss.
items.exampleCN: 超导性使电流可以无损耗地流动。

items.meaning: increased conductivity caused by light
items.meaningCN: 光电导性（photo-“光”+ conductivity）
items.example: Photoconductivity makes the sensor respond to bright light.
items.exampleCN: 光电导性使该传感器对强光作出反应。

items.meaning: the ease with which an object conducts current
items.meaningCN: 电导（-ance 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: The conductance of the thin film was measured at low voltage.
items.exampleCN: 在低电压下测量了这层薄膜的电导。

definition_zh: 配置；布局；构型；排列方式
definition_en: the way parts are arranged or set up, especially in a computer system or a physical structure
core_image: 按图纸把零件摆成一张互相连接的网
scene: In the server room, the engineer changed the configuration so that storage and network traffic no longer shared the same channel.
sceneCN: 这里 configuration 是「配置」（第 3 个义项：系统设置）；句意：机房里，工程师修改配置，使存储流量和网络流量不再共用同一通道。图中可辨识物件：机柜、服务器、网线、设置界面、标签。

pos.zh: 配置；布局；构型；排列方式

derivatives.zh: 已配置的；按特定方式设置的

senses.title: Arrangement of parts: layout
senses.titleCN: 排列方式/布局：部件如何摆
senses.definition: the way in which parts of something are arranged in relation to one another
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的各个部分相对于彼此摆放的方式
senses.example: The spatial configuration of the rooms makes the building easy to navigate.
senses.exampleCN: 房间的空间布局让这栋建筑很容易通行。
senses.why: configurare means 'to shape together', and -ation names the result of that shaping. A configuration is therefore the arrangement that results when parts are placed together.
senses.whyCN: configurare 意为“一起塑形”，-ation 命名塑形的结果。因此 configuration 就是把部件放在一起后形成的排列。

senses.title: Computer configuration
senses.titleCN: 计算机配置：硬件与软件的搭配
senses.definition: the combination of hardware and software settings that make up a computer setup
senses.definitionCN: 构成一台计算机系统的硬件与软件设置的组合
senses.example: This laptop's configuration includes 32 GB of memory and a 1 TB drive.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本电脑的配置包括 32 GB 内存和 1 TB 硬盘。
senses.why: The same result noun is applied to a machine: the parts and settings are 'shaped together' into one working setup, and -ation names that finished arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 同一个结果名词被用到机器上：部件与设置被“一起塑形”成一套可工作的系统，-ation 命名的正是这个完成的排列。

senses.title: System configuration
senses.titleCN: 系统配置：决定运行方式的设置组合
senses.definition: the set of settings that determines how a system behaves
senses.definitionCN: 决定一个系统如何运行的一组设置
senses.example: Changing the system configuration can affect how services start.
senses.exampleCN: 更改系统配置可能影响服务的启动方式。
senses.why: -ation here names an abstract arrangement rather than visible parts: settings are placed in relation to one another, and that arrangement controls behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ation 命名抽象排列而非可见部件：各项设置被摆放到彼此的关系中，而这个排列控制系统行为。

senses.title: Configuration file
senses.titleCN: 配置文件：存放设置的载体
senses.definition: a file that stores the settings of a program or system, often shortened to 'configuration' in IT speech
senses.definitionCN: 存放程序或系统设置的文件，在信息技术口语中常简称为 configuration
senses.example: Back up the configuration before you upgrade the router.
senses.exampleCN: 升级路由器之前先备份配置文件。
senses.why: This is metonymy: the file holds the configuration, so speakers name the container by its contents. The -ation noun itself still means the arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻：文件承载配置，于是说话者用内容来称呼容器。-ation 名词本身仍然表示“排列”。

senses.title: Spatial configuration
senses.titleCN: 空间构型：几何上的摆放关系
senses.definition: the geometric arrangement of points, lines, or objects in space
senses.definitionCN: 点、线或物体在空间中的几何排列
senses.example: The configuration of the three towers forms a triangle around the plaza.
senses.exampleCN: 三座塔楼的构型在广场周围形成一个三角形。
senses.why: Here figura is literal: the noun names the shape produced by placing objects at certain positions, with -ation marking the resulting form.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 figura 是字面意义：名词命名的是把物体放在特定位置后产生的形状，-ation 标记结果形态。

senses.title: Molecular configuration
senses.titleCN: 分子构型：原子在空间中的排布
senses.definition: the arrangement of atoms in a molecule in three-dimensional space
senses.definitionCN: 分子中原子在三维空间中的排列方式
senses.example: The two isomers differ only in their molecular configuration.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种异构体仅在分子构型上不同。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the noun for atoms 'shaped together'. The -ation result noun fits exactly: spatial placement of parts determines the molecule's identity.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用这个名词来描述原子被“一起塑形”。-ation 结果名词完全契合：部件在空间中的摆放决定分子的身份。

senses.title: Configuration management
senses.titleCN: 配置管理：让排列保持可控
senses.definition: the practice of recording, controlling, and tracking the settings of a system over time
senses.definitionCN: 对系统设置进行记录、控制和长期追踪的实践
senses.example: Configuration management keeps every server's settings under version control.
senses.exampleCN: 配置管理把每台服务器的设置都纳入版本控制。
senses.why: The noun becomes an object of management. -ation names a stable arrangement that can be recorded and changed deliberately, so it can be governed.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词成为管理的对象。-ation 命名一种可被记录、可被有意更改的稳定排列，因此可以被治理。

senses.title: Default configuration
senses.titleCN: 默认配置：初始的那套设置
senses.definition: the arrangement of settings that a product uses before the user changes anything
senses.definitionCN: 用户做出任何更改之前产品所使用的那套设置
senses.example: The app runs on its default configuration until you change it.
senses.exampleCN: 在你更改之前，这个应用一直运行在默认配置下。
senses.why: Default marks the arrangement set at the factory. The -ation noun is the same result noun, only fixed before the user begins to rearrange it.
senses.whyCN: default 标记出厂时设定的排列。这里的 -ation 仍是同一个结果名词，只是它在用户开始重新排列之前就已被固定。

senses.title: Network configuration
senses.titleCN: 网络配置：节点与地址的安排
senses.definition: the arrangement of devices, addresses, and connections in a network
senses.definitionCN: 网络中设备、地址和连接的安排方式
senses.example: A wrong network configuration left the printer offline.
senses.exampleCN: 错误的网络配置让打印机离线。
senses.why: The arrangement is now between devices rather than inside one machine, but -ation still names the way the parts are set in relation to one another.
senses.whyCN: 此时的排列发生在设备之间，而不是单台机器内部，但 -ation 仍然命名各部分彼此摆放的方式。

intro.en: Configuration is a three-stage derivative: Latin figura gives the idea of shape, configurare adds 'together', and -ation turns the verb into a noun. English technical uses are much later than the Latin base, and exact dates are approximate.
intro.cn: configuration 是分三步构成的派生词：拉丁 figura 提供“形状”观念，configurare 加上“一起”，-ation 再把动词变成名词。英语技术用法远晚于拉丁词基，确切年代为大致估计。

items.en: figura meant 'shape, form, figure'. The word begins with something visible that has an outline, not with an abstract plan.
items.cn: figura 意为“形状、外形、图形”。这个词的起点是一个有轮廓的可见之物，而不是抽象计划。

items.en: figurare meant 'to shape, form'. It turns the noun of shape into the act of giving shape.
items.cn: figurare 意为“使成形、塑造”。它把“形状”名词变成“赋予形状”的动作。

items.en: configurare adds con- 'together': to shape several things together, that is, to arrange them in relation to one another.
items.cn: configurare 加上 con-“一起”：把若干事物一起塑形，也就是按彼此的关系来安排它们。

items.en: English configure appears in the 17c. with the sense 'to form or arrange'. The verb is the base to which the noun suffix will attach.
items.cn: 英语 configure 在 17 世纪出现，意为“形成、安排”。这个动词就是名词后缀将要附着的词基。

items.en: configure + -ation, from Latin -atio(nem), forms a noun of process or result. Configuration is either the act of arranging or the arrangement that results.
items.cn: configure + -ation（来自拉丁 -atio(nem)）构成过程或结果名词。configuration 既可指安排的动作，也可指安排后的结果。

items.en: In 20c. computing the noun shifted toward stored settings: configuration file, system configuration, default configuration. Chemistry and IT management added molecular configuration and configuration management; exact first uses vary.
items.cn: 在 20 世纪的计算机领域，这个名词转向存储的设置：configuration file、system configuration、default configuration。化学和信息技术管理又加入 molecular configuration 与 configuration management；确切首次用法各异。

note.en: The look-alikes are other members of the configure family. The near-meaning words all describe how parts are placed, but each highlights a different aspect.
note.cn: 形近词是 configure 词族的其他成员。近义词都描述部件如何摆放，但各自突出不同侧面。

entries.definition: To set up or arrange parts for a particular purpose. It is the verb from which configuration is derived.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的设置或安排部件。它是 configuration 的派生来源动词。

entries.definition: Able to be configured or changed in arrangement. The -able suffix marks capacity, not the arrangement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 可配置的；排列可更改的。-able 后缀标记能力，而不是排列本身。

entries.definition: A tool or person that configures something, such as an online product configurator.
entries.definitionCN: 配置工具或配置者，如在线产品配置器。

entries.definition: The general way things are put in order or position. It is broader and less technical than configuration.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被排列或放置的一般方式。它比 configuration 更宽泛，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: The way a system or device is organized, or the act of preparing it. It is informal and common in everyday computing.
entries.definitionCN: 系统或设备的组织方式，或准备它的动作。它偏口语，常用于日常计算机语境。

entries.definition: The arrangement of physical elements on a page or in a space. It stresses visible placement.
entries.definitionCN: 物理元素在页面或空间中的布置。它强调可见的位置安排。

entries.definition: The way parts combine to form a whole. It stresses the mixture of components more than their precise placement.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分组合成整体的方式。它更强调成分的混合，而不是精确位置。

entries.definition: The three-dimensional shape adopted by a molecule. It is close to molecular configuration but often implies a shape that can change.
entries.definitionCN: 分子所采取的三维形状。它与 molecular configuration 接近，但常暗示形状可以改变。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root figura, the real suffix chain, and the real computing phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根 figura、真实的后缀链，以及真实的计算机搭配。

normal.en: con- 'together' + figura 'shape' + -ation: the noun is literally 'a shaping together'.
normal.cn: con-“一起”+ figura“形状”+ -ation：这个名词字面上就是“一起塑形”。

normal.en: A configuration file is the place where the arrangement is written down.
normal.cn: configuration file 就是把这个排列写下来的地方。

normal.en: Default configuration is the arrangement you get before you move anything.
normal.cn: default configuration 是你动手改动之前拿到的排列。

normal.en: Molecular configuration is the same idea at atomic scale: atoms placed in relation to one another.
normal.cn: molecular configuration 是同一观念在原子尺度上的版本：原子相对彼此摆放。

normal.en: Configuration management treats the arrangement as something that can be versioned and restored.
normal.cn: configuration management 把这种排列当作可以版本化、可以恢复的对象。

abstract.en: Think of LEGO bricks laid out according to a manual: the same bricks can make different objects depending on their configuration.
abstract.cn: 想象按说明书摆开的乐高积木：同样的积木因配置不同可以拼成不同物体。

abstract.en: Think of pins on a map connected by lines: the pins are the parts, and the web of lines is the configuration.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上用线连接起来的大头针：针是部件，线织成的网就是 configuration。

abstract.en: Think of a rack of servers with cables running between them: one wrong cable changes the whole arrangement.
abstract.cn: 想象一柜服务器之间连着的线缆：接错一根线就会改变整个排列。

examples.en: The configuration of the exhibition hall was changed to create wider walkways.
examples.cn: 展厅的布局被改动，以留出更宽的通道。

examples.en: You can restore the default configuration if the new settings cause problems.
examples.cn: 如果新设置引发问题，你可以恢复默认配置。

examples.en: The two molecules share the same formula but differ in configuration.
examples.cn: 这两个分子化学式相同，但构型不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯菲格蕾神”——肯（con）菲（fi）格（gu）蕾（ra）神（tion）按格子把零件摆好 → configuration 配置、布局

root: 拉丁 configurare“按形状摆好”（con-“一起”+ figurare“使成形”，figura“形状、外形”）；configure + -ation“过程或结果名词”。

sensesIntro.en: All nine senses are one noun seen from different angles: parts are shaped together, and the resulting arrangement can be physical, digital, or molecular.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都是同一个名词的不同观察角度：部件被一起塑形，而所得的排列可以是物理的、数字的或分子的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: parts placed together according to a plan until they form one connected shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：部件按图纸摆在一起，直到形成一个互相连接的整体形状。

branches.en: VISIBLE ARRANGEMENT: rooms, towers, and points form a layout or a geometric shape.
branches.cn: 可见排列：房间、塔楼和点构成布局或几何形状。

branches.en: MACHINE SETUP: hardware and software are arranged into a working setup, with a default state before changes.
branches.cn: 机器设置：硬件与软件被安排成可工作的组合，改动前有默认状态。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND NETWORK: settings or devices are placed in relation to one another and control how traffic flows.
branches.cn: 系统与网络：设置或设备彼此摆放，并控制流量如何流动。

branches.en: STORAGE: the arrangement is written into a file, and the container is named by its contents.
branches.cn: 存储：排列被写入文件，容器以内容命名。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND MANAGEMENT: atoms take a molecular shape, and the whole arrangement can be tracked and governed.
branches.cn: 科学与管理：原子形成分子形状，而整个排列可以被追踪和治理。

intro.en: Configuration is configure + -ation. -ation is the productive noun suffix of process or result; con- and figura are inherited inside the base and are not separately felt by most speakers.
intro.cn: configuration 是 configure + -ation。-ation 是表示过程或结果的能产名词后缀；con- 与 figura 已凝固在词基内部，多数说话者不会把它们单独拆开感受。

latinIntro.en: Latin figura 'shape' also gives figure, figurative, and figment; the verb figurare underlies configuration, transfiguration and disfigure. The family is about giving or changing form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 figura“形状”还衍生出 figure、figurative、figment；动词 figurare 是 configuration、transfiguration、disfigure 的基础。这个词族的核心是赋予或改变形式。

items.meaning: an arrangement of parts or settings
items.meaningCN: 配置；布局；构型（-ation 构成过程或结果名词）
items.example: The standard configuration suits most small offices.
items.exampleCN: 标准配置适合大多数小型办公室。

items.meaning: to arrange or set up parts
items.meaningCN: 配置；安排；设定（con-“一起”+ figurare“塑形”）
items.example: Configure the router before connecting it to the network.
items.exampleCN: 先把路由器配置好，再接入网络。

items.meaning: set up in a particular way
items.meaningCN: 已配置的；按特定方式设置的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The laptop is configured for video editing.
items.exampleCN: 这台笔记本电脑已按视频剪辑的需求配置好。

items.meaning: able to be arranged or changed
items.meaningCN: 可配置的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The keyboard shortcuts are fully configurable.
items.exampleCN: 键盘快捷键完全可配置。

items.meaning: a tool or person that configures
items.meaningCN: 配置器；配置者（-ator 表示施动者或工具）
items.example: The online configurator lets buyers choose every part.
items.exampleCN: 在线配置器让买家选择每一个部件。

items.meaning: a new arrangement after a change
items.meaningCN: 重新配置（re-“再次”+ configuration）
items.example: A reconfiguration of the network solved the bottleneck.
items.exampleCN: 网络的重新配置解决了瓶颈问题。

items.meaning: to set up in advance
items.meaningCN: 预配置（pre-“预先”+ configure）
items.example: The devices are preconfigured before they leave the factory.
items.exampleCN: 这些设备在出厂前已预配置好。

items.meaning: a wrong or faulty arrangement
items.meaningCN: 错误配置（mis-“错误地”+ configuration）
items.example: A misconfiguration exposed the database to the internet.
items.exampleCN: 一处错误配置让数据库暴露在互联网上。

items.meaning: a shape, a diagram, or a number
items.meaningCN: 形状；图形；数字（直接来自 figura）
items.example: The figure on the screen shows how the parts fit together.
items.exampleCN: 屏幕上的图形展示了各部件如何组合。

definition_zh: 确认；证实；确认函；坚振礼
definition_en: the act of confirming something, a message or document that confirms it, or the religious rite that strengthens a person's faith
core_image: 落下印章：把还悬着的事按实、定住
scene: After the guest paid the deposit, the hotel sent a confirmation with the room number and check-in time.
sceneCN: 这里 confirmation 是「预订确认」（第 5 个义项：预订确认函）；句意：客人付了定金后，酒店寄来一份写有房号和入住时间的确认函。图中可辨识物件：预订确认邮件、房号、入住时间、付款收据。

pos.zh: 确认；证实；确认的行为
确认函；确认书；（宗教）坚振礼

collocations.zh: 确认偏误（只找支持自己看法的证据）

senses.title: The act of making something certain
senses.titleCN: 确认行为：把不确定变为确定
senses.definition: the act of showing that something is true, valid, or definitely arranged
senses.definitionCN: 证明某事为真、有效或已经确定的行为
senses.example: The lab asked for confirmation of the results before publication.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室要求在发表前先确认这些结果。
senses.why: confirmare is con- 'thoroughly' plus firmare 'to make firm', from firmus 'firm'. The suffix -ation turns that act into a noun, so confirmation is literally 'the making-firm' — the act itself, before it names any document.
senses.whyCN: confirmare 是 con-“彻底”加 firmare“使坚固”，后者出自 firmus“坚固”。后缀 -ation 把这个动作变成名词，因此 confirmation 字面上就是“使坚固这件事”——先指行为本身，还不指任何文件。

senses.title: A message that confirms
senses.titleCN: 确认邮件或确认消息
senses.definition: an email, letter, or message that states that an arrangement is definite
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项安排已经确定的邮件、信件或消息
senses.example: She received a confirmation within minutes of booking the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 她订完机票几分钟后就收到了确认消息。
senses.why: Action nouns in -ation can name the result as well as the act. Once the making-firm is finished, the thing that carries it — the message — is also called a confirmation, because the paper or email now holds the firmness.
senses.whyCN: -ation 类动作名词既能指行为，也能指结果。一旦“使坚固”完成，承载它的东西——那条消息——也被叫作 confirmation，因为纸张或邮件此时替人保存了这份确定。

senses.title: Confirmation bias: the mind proving itself right
senses.titleCN: 确认偏误：只找支持自己的证据
senses.definition: the tendency to notice and trust information that supports what one already believes
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于注意并相信支持自己既有看法的信息
senses.example: Confirmation bias led the team to notice only the data that supported its plan.
senses.exampleCN: 确认偏误让团队只注意到支持自己计划的数据。
senses.why: This 20c psychological term keeps the 'making firm' image but turns it inward: the mind seeks evidence that firms up a belief it already holds. Here confirmation is not a message from outside but an act of self-reinforcement.
senses.whyCN: 这个 20 世纪的心理学词保留了“使坚固”的意象，却把它转向内部：心智去寻找能让既有信念更坚固的证据。这里的 confirmation 不是外来消息，而是一种自我加固的动作。

senses.title: A hearing that confirms an appointment
senses.titleCN: 任命确认听证会
senses.definition: a formal hearing in which a committee examines a nominee before approving the appointment
senses.definitionCN: 委员会在批准任命前审查被提名者的正式听证会
senses.example: The senate held a confirmation hearing for the new judge.
senses.exampleCN: 参议院为这位新法官举行了确认听证会。
senses.why: In this political branch, 'make firm' is applied to a person's official standing: the nominee is not securely in office until the appointment is confirmed. The hearing is the procedure that produces that firmness.
senses.whyCN: 在这一政治分支里，“使坚固”作用于一个人的官方地位：任命未经确认，被提名者就还没有稳稳地进入职位。听证会就是产生这份确定性的程序。

senses.title: A booking confirmed in writing
senses.titleCN: 预订确认函
senses.definition: a document or message that proves a reservation, ticket, or booking is final
senses.definitionCN: 证明预订、机票或订房已经最终生效的文件或消息
senses.example: Keep your confirmation in case the front desk cannot find the reservation.
senses.exampleCN: 把确认函留着，以防前台找不到这条预订记录。
senses.why: The commercial sense is 20c: a reservation stays provisional until the hotel makes it firm in writing. The document that performs this act then takes the name of the act itself, a common pattern in travel and booking language.
senses.whyCN: 商业义是 20 世纪的产物：预订在酒店以书面方式将其“定实”之前都只是暂定的。完成这一动作的文件于是直接继承了动作的名字，这在旅游和预订用语中很常见。

senses.title: The sacrament that strengthens faith
senses.titleCN: 坚振礼：坚固信仰的圣礼
senses.definition: a religious rite in which a baptized person affirms their faith and is said to receive strength from the Holy Spirit
senses.definitionCN: 受洗者确认自己的信仰、并被认为从圣灵获得力量的宗教仪式
senses.example: In some churches, young people receive confirmation at about thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些教会里，年轻人十三岁左右接受坚振礼。
senses.why: The religious sense is the oldest in English, recorded in the 13c. Latin firmare also meant 'strengthen', so confirmation became the sacrament that strengthens baptismal faith. The original metaphor of making firm is here applied to a person's belief.
senses.whyCN: 宗教义是英语里最古老的一支，13 世纪已有记录。拉丁语 firmare 同时有“使强壮”之意，因此 confirmation 成了坚固受洗信仰的圣礼。原本“使坚固”的比喻在这里落到了人的信念上。

senses.title: A receipt that confirms payment
senses.titleCN: 收据确认：证明款项已付
senses.definition: a receipt or stamp that officially acknowledges that money has been paid
senses.definitionCN: 正式承认款项已付的收据或印章
senses.example: The cashier stamped the receipt as confirmation of payment.
senses.exampleCN: 收银员在收据上盖章，作为付款确认。
senses.why: Here -ation again names the concrete evidence of an act: the stamped receipt is the making-firm of a payment, proof that the transaction will not be reopened. The thing that fixes the record borrows the name of the fixing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ation 又指动作的具体证据：盖了章的收据就是付款的“使坚固”，是这笔交易不会再有争议的证明。固定记录的那件东西，借用了“固定”这个动作的名字。

senses.title: A test that confirms an earlier result
senses.titleCN: 验证性测试：二次确认
senses.definition: a second test carried out to check a provisional result from an earlier test
senses.definitionCN: 为检查先前初步结果而进行的第二次测试
senses.example: A confirmatory test was run after the first screen gave a faint line.
senses.exampleCN: 初筛出现浅线后，又做了一次验证性测试。
senses.why: Confirmatory is confirm plus -atory 'serving to'. A confirmatory test is a second act of making firm, ordered precisely because the first result was not yet firm. Confirmation here names that second stage rather than a document.
senses.whyCN: confirmatory 是 confirm 加 -atory“用于……的”。验证性测试就是第二次“使坚固”，之所以要做，正是因为第一次结果还不够牢靠。这里的 confirmation 指那个第二阶段，而不是文件。

senses.title: An official statement by an authority
senses.titleCN: 官方确认：权威机构的正式声明
senses.definition: a public statement from an official body that settles a report or rumour
senses.definitionCN: 官方机构就某报道或传言作出的、使其尘埃落定的公开声明
senses.example: The ministry issued an official confirmation of the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部发布了关于这次疫情的官方确认。
