senses.title: Considerably better: a wide margin of improvement
senses.titleCN: 明显更好：改进幅度很大
senses.definition: much better than something else, so that the difference is easy to notice
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物好得多，差别很容易被察觉
senses.example: The revised manuscript is considerably better than the first draft.
senses.exampleCN: 修改后的稿子比初稿明显更好。
senses.why: When -ly modifies a comparative such as better, the 'worth noticing' idea attaches to the gap between the two things. A considerable gap is one large enough to be seen, not a marginal one.
senses.whyCN: 当 -ly 修饰 better 这类比较级时，“值得注意”落在两个事物之间的差距上。considerable 的差距就是大到看得见的差距，而不是微小的差别。

senses.title: Considerably more: a large increase in quantity
senses.titleCN: 明显更多：数量增加很多
senses.definition: a much larger amount or number than before or than something else
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目比以前或比另一事物大得多
senses.example: This model consumes considerably more power than that one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个型号比那个型号耗电多得多。
senses.why: The same degree suffix is applied to more. The quantity is not merely higher but higher by an amount worth registering, which is exactly what -able contributed to the base word.
senses.whyCN: 同一个程度后缀加在 more 上。数量不只是更高，而是高到“值得记录”的程度，这正是 -able 给词根带来的那层意思。

senses.title: Considerably less: a large reduction in quantity
senses.titleCN: 明显更少：数量减少很多
senses.definition: a much smaller amount or number than before or than something else
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目比以前或比另一事物少得多
senses.example: The second design costs considerably less to produce.
senses.exampleCN: 第二种设计的生产成本低得多。
senses.why: Degree words are direction-neutral: the -ly adverb measures the size of the difference, not whether it goes up or down. With less, the same 'notable gap' reading points downward.
senses.whyCN: 程度词本身不分方向：-ly 副词衡量的是差距的大小，而不是差距向上还是向下。与 less 搭配时，同一个“显著差距”就指向减少。

senses.title: Considerably reduce: cut something by a large amount
senses.titleCN: 大幅降低：大量削减
senses.definition: to make something smaller or lower by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物在数量或水平上大幅下降
senses.example: The company reduced its carbon emissions considerably by switching to solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 公司改用太阳能后大幅降低了碳排放。
senses.why: Here the adverb modifies a verb of change. The -able base supplies the idea of a noticeable amount, and -ly presents that amount as the manner or extent of the reducing action.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词修饰变化动词。-able 词基提供“显著数量”的意思，-ly 则把这个数量呈现为“削减”这一动作的程度。

senses.title: Considerably increase: raise something by a large amount
senses.titleCN: 大幅增加：大量提高
senses.definition: to make something larger or higher by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物在数量或水平上大幅上升
senses.example: Demand for the product increased considerably after the advertising campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 广告活动之后，产品的需求大幅增加。
senses.why: Increase and reduce are opposite verbs, yet considerably qualifies both because it measures extent rather than direction. This is the adverb's core function inherited from considerable 'large in extent'.
senses.whyCN: increase 与 reduce 是相反动词，却都能被 considerably 修饰，因为它衡量的是程度而不是方向。这正是 considerable“程度大”这一核心义赋予副词的用法。

senses.title: Differ considerably: be very different
senses.titleCN: 大不相同：差异显著
senses.definition: to be very different from one another in a noticeable way
senses.definitionCN: 彼此之间有明显差异
senses.example: The two dialects differ considerably in pronunciation.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种方言在发音上差异很大。
senses.why: Difference is a gap, and the -able element originally marked something worth noticing. Differ considerably therefore says the gap is wide enough to deserve attention.
senses.whyCN: 差异就是一道缝隙，而 -able 成分原本表示“值得注意”。differ considerably 因而表示这道缝隙宽到值得关注。

senses.title: Considerably larger: much bigger in size
senses.titleCN: 大得多：尺寸明显更大
senses.definition: much greater in size, extent, or capacity
senses.definitionCN: 在尺寸、范围或容量上大得多
senses.example: The new hall is considerably larger than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新大厅比旧大厅大得多。
senses.why: Larger is a comparative of size. The -ly adverb says the size difference is not slight; it inherits the 'large, substantial' sense that considerable developed from 'worthy of consideration'.
senses.whyCN: larger 是尺寸比较级。-ly 副词说明尺寸差距并不轻微；它继承了 considerable 从“值得考虑”发展出的“大而可观”之义。

senses.title: Considerably affect: influence something strongly
senses.titleCN: 显著影响：对某事产生较大作用
senses.definition: to have a strong influence on something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或某人产生较大影响
senses.example: Rising rents have considerably affected young families in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 不断上涨的房租显著影响了城里的年轻家庭。
senses.why: Affect is about the force of an influence. Adding considerably turns a neutral statement of influence into one about the size of the effect, again the degree sense carried by -ly from considerable.
senses.whyCN: affect 讲的是影响力的作用。加上 considerably，就把中性的“有影响”变成“影响程度很大”，这仍是由 -ly 从 considerable 带来的程度义。

intro.en: Considerably is a three-step derivative: consider + -able + -ly. Dates are approximate, and the famous 'star' explanation of consider is uncertain.
intro.cn: considerably 是三步派生：consider + -able + -ly。年代为大致估计；consider 那个著名的“观星”解释并不确定。

items.en: The base is Latin considerare 'to look at closely, examine, observe'. English consider is recorded in the late 14c. with the sense 'to examine, think about'.
items.cn: 基础词是拉丁语 considerare“仔细察看、审视、观察”。英语 consider 在 14 世纪晚期被记录，意为“审视、思考”。

items.en: Considerare is usually analyzed as com- 'together' + sidus 'star, constellation', picturing the observation of stars to read omens. This explanation is uncertain and is not treated here as established fact.
items.cn: considerare 通常被分析为 com-“一起” + sidus“星、星座”，描绘观星以定吉凶。这一解释来源不确定，此处不当作已确证的事实。

items.en: Consider + -able (through Old French -able, from Latin -abilis) produced considerable in the 15c., first meaning 'able to be considered, worthy of consideration'.
items.cn: consider + -able（经由古法语 -able，源自拉丁语 -abilis）在 15 世纪产生 considerable，最初意为“能被考虑的、值得考虑的”。

items.en: From 'worthy of consideration' the adjective moved to 'large enough to be noticed, substantial'. What deserves attention becomes what has noticeable size or degree; the modern quantitative sense is established by the 18c.
items.cn: 从“值得考虑”转为“大到值得注意的、可观的”。值得关注的东西变成了有显著规模或程度的东西；现代的数量义在 18 世纪确立。

items.en: Considerable + -ly (Old English -lice) formed considerably, 'in a considerable manner or degree'. The suffix converts the adjective's size judgment into an adverb measuring how much an action or quality extends.
items.cn: considerable + -ly（古英语 -lice）构成 considerably，意为“以可观的的方式或程度”。后缀把形容词的“大小判断”转成副词，用来衡量动作或性质延伸到什么程度。

items.en: Modern usage specializes the word as a degree booster with comparatives (considerably better, larger) and change verbs (increase, reduce, differ). The family also includes consideration, considerate and inconsiderable.
items.cn: 现代用法把它专作程度加强词，常搭配比较级（considerably better、larger）和变化动词（increase、reduce、differ）。同族词还包括 consideration、considerate、inconsiderable。

note.en: The first group holds spelling neighbours from the same consider family; the second holds words that also express a large degree.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 consider 词族中拼写相近的词；第二组是同样表达“程度大”的近义词。

entries.definition: large in amount or degree. It is the adjective that considerably is built from, not an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度大的。它是 considerably 所由构成的形容词，不是副词。

entries.definition: thoughtful about other people's feelings. It comes from consider in the older sense 'think about others'.
entries.definitionCN: 体贴的，顾及他人感受的。它来自 consider 较旧的“替别人着想”之义。

entries.definition: taking something into account, as in 'considering the weather'. It is not a degree word.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑到……，如 considering the weather。它不是程度词。

entries.definition: to a notable degree, often used of measurable or statistical change. It is more technical than considerably.
entries.definitionCN: 达到显著程度，常用于可测量或统计上的变化。它比 considerably 更偏技术。

entries.definition: to a large degree, especially of amounts, costs, or changes. It often sounds more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上，尤用于数量、成本或变化。它通常更正式。

entries.definition: very much. It is formal and common with verbs of feeling, change, or appreciation.
entries.definitionCN: 非常、大大地。它较正式，常与情感、变化或感激类动词搭配。

entries.definition: in a way that is easy to notice or distinguish. It stresses visibility of the difference.
entries.definitionCN: 以明显、容易察觉的方式。它强调差异的可见性。

entries.definition: by a great amount, used with comparatives as in 'far better'. It is shorter and more idiomatic than considerably.
entries.definitionCN: 大大地，用于比较级，如 far better。它比 considerably 更短、更口语化。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real consider family, the real suffix chain, and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 consider 词族、真实的后缀链条和真实搭配。

normal.en: consider + able: something considerable is literally 'able to be considered', hence worth noticing. Add -ly and it means 'to a noticeable degree'.
normal.cn: consider + able：considerable 字面是“能被考虑的”，也就是“值得注意的”。再加 -ly，就是“达到值得注意的程度”。

normal.en: Keep the pair straight: considerable is the adjective, considerably is the adverb. You say 'a considerable rise' but 'prices rose considerably'.
normal.cn: 把一对词分清：considerable 是形容词，considerably 是副词。说 a considerable rise，但说 prices rose considerably。

normal.en: The common frames are change verbs plus considerably: rise, increase, reduce, differ, vary, affect.
normal.cn: 常见框架是变化动词 + considerably：rise、increase、reduce、differ、vary、affect。

normal.en: The family tree is consider → considerable → considerably, with consideration and considerate branching off the same base.
normal.cn: 词族树是 consider → considerable → considerably，consideration 与 considerate 从同一词基分出。

normal.en: With comparatives, read it as 'a wide margin': considerably better means the gap is large enough to see, not just slightly better.
normal.cn: 与比较级连用时把它读作“差距很大”：considerably better 指差距大到看得见，而不只是稍好一点。

abstract.en: Picture a dial: consider is the careful look, -able says the amount is worth looking at, and -ly moves the needle several marks past the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个刻度盘：consider 是仔细察看，-able 表示这个量值得一看，-ly 则让指针越过基准线好几格。

abstract.en: The word is a magnifier, not a direction. It can sit on better or worse, more or less, because it measures the width of the gap.
abstract.cn: 这个词是放大镜，不是方向标。它可以配 better 或 worse、more 或 less，因为它衡量的是差距的宽度。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps one claim: the difference is big enough that ignoring it would be a mistake.
abstract.cn: 所有义项都保留一个主张：这个差别大到若忽视它就会出错。

examples.en: Housing costs rose considerably after the factory opened.
examples.cn: 工厂开办后，住房成本大幅上升。

examples.en: The new engine is considerably more efficient than the old one.
examples.cn: 新发动机比旧发动机效率高得多。

examples.en: The two plans differ considerably in cost and risk.
examples.cn: 这两个方案在成本和风险上差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯细得若伯利”——肯细细地算，得的伯利（利润）相当大 → considerably 相当大地

root: consider（拉丁 considerare“仔细察看”）+ -able（值得……的）+ -ly（副词后缀）：从“值得考虑”转为“程度大到值得注意”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of considerably all carry one signal: the extent or gap is large enough to notice. The direction comes from the word it modifies, not from the adverb itself.
sensesIntro.cn: considerably 的九个义项都发出同一个信号：程度或差距大到值得注意。方向来自它所修饰的词，而不是副词本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial needle jumping several marks past the baseline.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度盘指针一次越过基准线好几格。

branches.en: GENERAL DEGREE: a plain statement that something is true to a large extent.
branches.cn: 一般程度：直接说明某事在很大程度上成立。

branches.en: COMPARISON: better or larger by a margin wide enough to see.
branches.cn: 比较：更好或更大，差距宽到看得见。

branches.en: QUANTITY: more or less by a substantial amount.
branches.cn: 数量：多或少都达到可观的幅度。

branches.en: CHANGE: reducing or increasing something by a large amount.
branches.cn: 变化：大幅削减或大幅提高。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE AND IMPACT: a wide gap between things, or a strong effect on them.
branches.cn: 差异与影响：事物之间差距很大，或对之产生很大作用。

intro.en: Considerably stacks two suffixes on a Latin verb: -able makes an adjective of 'worth considering', and -ly turns that adjective into a degree adverb. Neither suffix changes the base meaning; each changes the word class.
intro.cn: considerably 在拉丁动词上叠加两个后缀：-able 把“值得考虑”做成形容词，-ly 再把这个形容词变成程度副词。两个后缀都不改变词基意义，只改变词性。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is considerare and its disputed parts com- and sidus. The suffix -abilis supplied English -able; -ly is native English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 considerare 及其有争议的成分 com- 与 sidus。后缀 -abilis 提供英语 -able；-ly 是英语本族后缀，不是拉丁语。

items.meaning: large enough to be noticed; substantial
items.meaningCN: 相当大的；可观的（-able 构成“能被……的”形容词）
items.example: The project required a considerable investment.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目需要相当大的投资。

items.meaning: to a large degree
items.meaningCN: 相当大地（-ly 把形容词转为程度副词）
items.example: The situation has improved considerably.
items.exampleCN: 情况已大幅好转。

items.meaning: too small to matter
items.meaningCN: 微不足道的（in- 否定 -able 的“值得考虑”）
items.example: The sum was not inconsiderable.
items.exampleCN: 这笔钱可不是小数目。

items.meaning: the act of thinking about something; care for others
items.meaningCN: 考虑；体谅（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: After careful consideration, they chose the cheaper plan.
items.exampleCN: 仔细考虑后，他们选择了较便宜的方案。

items.meaning: thoughtful about other people
items.meaningCN: 体贴的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: It was considerate of you to call ahead.
items.exampleCN: 你提前打电话，真是体贴。

items.meaning: not thinking about other people's feelings
items.meaningCN: 不体贴的；不顾他人的（in- 否定）
items.example: Loud music late at night is inconsiderate.
items.exampleCN: 深夜大声放音乐是不顾及他人的。

items.meaning: in a thoughtful way
items.meaningCN: 体贴地（形容词 + -ly 构成副词）
items.example: She considerately left the light on for him.
items.exampleCN: 她体贴地为他留了灯。

items.meaning: to think about something again
items.meaningCN: 重新考虑（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: Please reconsider your decision.
items.exampleCN: 请重新考虑你的决定。

items.meaning: taking something into account
items.meaningCN: 考虑到（-ing 分词转化为介词）
items.example: Considering the rain, we stayed indoors.
items.exampleCN: 考虑到下雨，我们留在室内。

latinEntries.meaning: to examine closely, observe, think over

latinEntries.meaningCN: 星、星座（consider 的词源分析有争议）

definition_zh: 一致性；连贯性；稳定度；（混合物的）均匀度、浓稠度
definition_en: the quality of staying the same over time, or of having parts that agree with one another
core_image: 同一桶颜料反复倒出，每次颜色与质地都分毫不差
scene: Before shipping the sauce, the chef checks the consistency of every batch with a spoon.
sceneCN: 这里 consistency 是「（酱料的）均匀度、浓稠度」（第 5 个义项：质地均匀度）；句意：发货前，厨师用勺子检查每一批酱料的浓稠度是否均匀。图中可辨识物件：酱料桶、勺子、批次标签、记录表。

pos.zh: 一致性；连贯性；稳定度；均匀度

senses.title: Agreement: the state of staying the same
senses.titleCN: 一致性：前后相同的状态
senses.definition: the quality of remaining the same, or of agreeing with something else
senses.definitionCN: 保持不变或与其他事物相符合的性质
senses.example: There is no consistency between his words and his actions.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言行之间没有一致性。
senses.why: Consistency is consist + -ency. Latin consistere meant 'to stand together, stand firm'; parts that stand together hold one shape. The -ency suffix names that state, so consistency is the quality of standing together without breaking apart.
senses.whyCN: consistency 是 consist + -ency。拉丁语 consistere 意为“站在一起、站稳”；能站在一起的各部分保持着同一形态。-ency 命名这种状态，所以 consistency 就是“站在一起而不散开”的性质。

senses.title: Consistency of results: repeated trials agree
senses.titleCN: 结果一致性：多次试验相互吻合
senses.definition: the degree to which repeated measurements or experiments give the same result
senses.definitionCN: 重复测量或实验给出相同结果的程度
senses.example: The team ran the test five times to check the consistency of the results.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把测试跑了五遍，以检查结果是否一致。
senses.why: Each new result is a thing that must 'stand together' with the previous ones. When they all line up, the run has consistency; a result that falls out of line breaks the standing-together relation.
senses.whyCN: 每一个新结果都是必须与前几次“站在一起”的东西。当它们排成同一条线时，这一轮试验就有一致性；偏离的结果则破坏了这种并立关系。

senses.title: Consistency of behaviour: acting the same way
senses.titleCN: 行为一贯性：以同样的方式行事
senses.definition: the quality of behaving in the same way on different occasions
senses.definitionCN: 在不同场合以相同方式行事的品质
senses.example: Her consistency in arriving early earned her a promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 她一贯早到，这为她赢得了晋升。
senses.why: A person's actions over time are the parts that must stand together. The same person repeating the same conduct makes those actions cohere, so the moral and practical sense grows directly from consistere 'stand firm'.
senses.whyCN: 一个人历时的行为就是必须彼此并立的“各部分”。同一个人重复同样的举动，使这些行为连贯起来，因此这一行为义直接从 consistere“站稳”生长出来。

senses.title: Logical consistency: no contradiction
senses.titleCN: 逻辑一致性：没有自相矛盾
senses.definition: the state in which statements or reasons do not contradict one another
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或理由之间互不矛盾的状态
senses.example: A good argument needs logical consistency from premise to conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好的论证从前提 到结论都需要逻辑一致性。
senses.why: Propositions stand together when none knocks another down. The Latin image of parts standing firm becomes, in reasoning, the requirement that every claim supports rather than contradicts the rest.
senses.whyCN: 命题彼此并立，就是没有一个把另一个推翻。拉丁语“各部分站稳”的形象，在推理中就变成“每个主张支持而非反驳其余主张”的要求。

senses.title: Texture: the evenness of a mixture
senses.titleCN: 质地均匀度：混合物的稠稀与均匀
senses.definition: the thickness, smoothness, or evenness of a liquid or soft mixture
senses.definitionCN: 液体或软质混合物的浓稠度、细腻度或均匀程度
senses.example: Add water until the batter reaches the consistency of thick cream.
senses.exampleCN: 加水直到面糊达到浓奶油的稠度。
senses.why: Latin consistere also meant 'to be composed of, to have firmness'. A sauce that 'stands together' has the same texture throughout. The physical branch keeps the oldest literal sense of standing firm.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 consistere 也有“由……构成、具有硬度”的意思。能“站在一起”的酱料，整体质地相同。这一物质分支保留了“站稳”最古老的字面义。

senses.title: Consistency check: testing that parts still agree
senses.titleCN: 一致性检查：检验各部分是否仍然吻合
senses.definition: a test that verifies whether stored data or system parts still match one another
senses.definitionCN: 检验存储数据或系统各部分是否仍相互吻合的检查
senses.example: The software runs a consistency check before it saves the database.
senses.exampleCN: 软件在保存数据库之前会运行一致性检查。
senses.why: A check asks whether the parts can still stand together. The noun is used attributively, like a label on the procedure, but the underlying idea is still the -ency state of coherent parts.
senses.whyCN: 检查要问的是各部分是否仍能站在一起。这里名词作定语，像程序上的标签，但底层仍是 -ency 所表示的“部分彼此连贯”的状态。

senses.title: Long-term stability: sameness across time
senses.titleCN: 长期稳定性：长时间保持不变
senses.definition: the quality of remaining reliable and unchanged over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在长时间内保持可靠、不发生变化的品质
senses.example: The drug's long-term consistency makes it reliable for daily use.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物的长期稳定性使其适合每日使用。
senses.why: Standing firm is a matter of time as much as of shape. When the same effect holds across years, the parts keep standing together; the temporal reading is an extension of the base verb's 'stand firm'.
senses.whyCN: “站稳”既是形态问题，也是时间问题。当同一效果多年保持，各部分就一直并立；这一时间义是基础动词“站稳”的延伸。

senses.title: Internal consistency: the parts measure one thing
senses.titleCN: 内部一致性：各部分指向同一对象
senses.definition: the degree to which the items within a test or document agree with one another
senses.definitionCN: 测试或文件内部各项目彼此吻合的程度
senses.example: The survey showed high internal consistency across its twenty questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查的二十个问题表现出很高的内部一致性。
senses.why: Internal shifts the focus inside one instrument: its items are the parts that must stand together. High internal consistency means the questions are all pulling in the same direction, like poles standing in one line.
senses.whyCN: internal 把焦点移到同一工具内部：它的各个项目就是必须并立的“部分”。内部一致性高，意味着所有问题都朝同一方向用力，像一根根立在同一线上的杆子。

senses.title: Consistency standard: a rule requiring sameness
senses.titleCN: 一致性标准：要求保持相同的准则
senses.definition: an agreed rule or benchmark that requires decisions or outputs to remain the same
senses.definitionCN: 要求决定或产出保持相同的一致规则或基准
senses.example: The league introduced a consistency standard for referees' decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 联赛为裁判判罚引入了一致性标准。
senses.why: Here the noun modifies 'standard': it names the property the rule demands. The -ency noun of state is turned into a measurable requirement, but the content is still 'things must stand together'.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词修饰 standard：它命名规则所要求的性质。-ency 的状态名词被转成可衡量的要求，但内容仍是“事物必须站在一起”。

intro.en: Consistency is consist + -ency. The base is Latin consistere 'to stand firm, be composed of'. Dates are approximate; the physical and abstract senses developed side by side.
intro.cn: consistency 是 consist + -ency。基础词是拉丁语 consistere“站稳、由……构成”。年代为大致估计；物质义与抽象义是并行发展出来的。

items.en: The base verb is consistere, 'to take one's stand, stand firm; to be composed of'. English consist is borrowed from it and first means 'to have a settled position' before 'to be made up of'.
items.cn: 基础动词是 consistere“站定、站稳；由……构成”。英语 consist 借自它，先有“占据稳定位置”之义，后发展出“由……组成”。

items.en: Consistere is con- 'together' + sistere 'to stand, stand still'. Sistere is related to stare 'to stand', so the picture is several things taking a position together and holding it.
items.cn: consistere 是 con-“一起” + sistere“站立、站住”。sistere 与 stare“站立”同源，因此画面是若干事物一起就位并保持住。

items.en: Consist + -ency (from Latin -entia through French -ence) formed consistency, a noun of state: 'the condition of standing together'. The suffix adds no new meaning; it turns the verb's state into an abstract quality.
items.cn: consist + -ency（经法语 -ence 来自拉丁语 -entia）构成 consistency，这是状态名词：“站在一起的状态”。后缀不增添新义，只把动词的状态转成抽象性质。

items.en: Early English uses cover both 'firmness, density' of a substance and 'agreement, harmony' of parts. The physical sense is not a later metaphor; it preserves the literal 'stand firm / be composed of'.
items.cn: 早期英语用法同时包括物质的“硬度、密度”和部分的“一致、和谐”。物质义不是后来的比喻，而是保留了“站稳／由……构成”的字面义。

items.en: As the word moved into argument, conduct and data, the concrete image faded: what stands together became what agrees. The texture sense stayed in cooking and chemistry, while the abstract sense generalized to logic and behaviour.
items.cn: 当这个词进入论证、行为和数据领域，具体形象淡化了：站在一起的东西变成了相互吻合的东西。质地义留在烹饪与化学中，抽象义则扩展到逻辑与行为。

items.en: Modern usage measures consistency: high or low internal consistency, consistency of results, consistency checks. The -ency noun now functions as a countable and uncountable quality noun with a technical edge.
items.cn: 现代用法对 consistency 进行度量：内部一致性高低、结果一致性、一致性检查。-ency 名词现在既是可数又可不可数的性质名词，并带技术色彩。

note.en: The first group contains words that look or sound close to consistency; the second contains nouns with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音接近 consistency 的词；第二组是意思相近的名词。

entries.definition: to be made up of particular parts. It is the verb behind consistency, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定部分构成。它是 consistency 背后的动词，不是名词。

entries.definition: an older variant of consistency, now rare and mostly limited to the physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: consistency 的旧变体，现已罕用，多限于物质义。

entries.definition: a voting district or the voters in it. It belongs to constituent, not to consist.
entries.definitionCN: 选区或该区的选民。它属于 constituent，而不是 consist。

entries.definition: the quality of parts fitting together clearly and logically. It stresses intelligible connection, while consistency stresses sameness.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分清晰、合逻辑地结合在一起的品质。它强调可理解的关联，而 consistency 强调相同。

entries.definition: the state of being the same in form or character. It is closer to 'identical' than consistency is.
entries.definitionCN: 在形式或性质上相同的状态。它比 consistency 更接近“完全一样”。

entries.definition: the quality of staying steady and not changing. It emphasizes resistance to disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 保持平稳、不改变的性质。它强调抵抗干扰的能力。

entries.definition: the quality of remaining the same or loyal over time. It is more literary and personal than consistency.
entries.definitionCN: 随着时间保持相同或忠诚的品质。它比 consistency 更文学化、更偏个人情感。

entries.definition: the state of matching or having the same opinion. It is broader and less technical than consistency.
entries.definitionCN: 相互吻合或意见相同的状态。它比 consistency 更宽泛、更不技术化。

normalIntro.en: These links use the real consist family, the real -ency suffix, and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联系使用真实的 consist 词族、真实的 -ency 后缀和真实搭配。

normal.en: consist means 'stand together'. Add -ency and you get the state of standing together: consistency.
normal.cn: consist 意为“站在一起”。加上 -ency，就得到“站在一起的状态”：consistency。

normal.en: The family is easy to hold in one line: consist → consistent → consistently → consistency, with in- negating the last three.
normal.cn: 这个词族可以串成一条线：consist → consistent → consistently → consistency，而 in- 否定后三个。

normal.en: The physical sense survives in the kitchen: whisk the sauce to the right consistency.
normal.cn: 物质义仍活在厨房里：把酱汁搅到合适的浓稠度。

normal.en: Typical frames: maintain consistency, achieve consistency, internal consistency, consistency check, consistency of results.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：maintain consistency、achieve consistency、internal consistency、consistency check、consistency of results。

normal.en: -ency marks a noun of state or quality, as in frequency and agency. Here the state is 'not changing'.
normal.cn: -ency 标记状态或性质名词，如 frequency、agency。这里的状态是“不改变”。

abstract.en: Picture several poles standing in one straight line. As long as none leans, they are consistent; one leaning pole is an inconsistency.
abstract.cn: 想象几根杆子立成一条直线。只要没有一根倾斜，它们就是一致的；一根倾斜的杆子就是一处不一致。

abstract.en: Pour the same mixture twice and compare the texture. The sameness you feel is consistency in its oldest physical sense.
abstract.cn: 把同一混合物倒两次，比较质地。你摸到的那种相同感，就是 consistency 最古老的物质义。

abstract.en: Across all nine senses one test remains: do the parts still stand together, or has something broken the line?
abstract.cn: 九个义项共用同一个检验：各部分是否仍站在一起，还是有东西破坏了这条线？

examples.en: The report found a lack of consistency between the two data sets.
examples.cn: 报告发现两组数据之间缺乏一致性。

examples.en: Whisk the sauce until its consistency is smooth and even.
examples.cn: 把酱汁搅打至质地细腻均匀。

examples.en: Her consistency in training explains her steady improvement.
examples.cn: 她训练的一贯性解释了她为何能稳步进步。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯细思坦西”——肯细细思量，站得稳、前后不变 → consistency 一致性

root: consist（拉丁 consistere“站在一起、站稳”）+ -ency（名词后缀）：由“站得住”转为“前后一致、质地均匀”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of consistency all test one thing: whether parts stand together. The parts may be statements, results, actions, measurements, or the texture of a mixture.
sensesIntro.cn: consistency 的九个义项都在检验同一件事：各部分是否站在一起。这些部分可以是陈述、结果、行为、测量数据，或混合物的质地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same mixture poured twice, identical in colour and texture.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一桶颜料反复倒出，颜色与质地分毫不差。

branches.en: AGREEMENT AND STANDARD: general sameness, and the rule that demands it.
branches.cn: 一致与标准：总体上的相同，以及要求相同的规则。

branches.en: RESULTS AND CHECKS: repeated outputs agree, and a procedure verifies that they still do.
branches.cn: 结果与检查：重复产出相互吻合，并有程序检验它们仍然吻合。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR OVER TIME: the same conduct repeated, and reliability across a long period.
branches.cn: 历时的行为：重复同样的举动，以及在长时间内的可靠性。

branches.en: LOGIC AND INTERNAL STRUCTURE: claims do not contradict, and items inside one instrument point the same way.
branches.cn: 逻辑与内部结构：主张互不矛盾，同一工具内部各项目指向同一方向。

branches.en: PHYSICAL TEXTURE: the oldest concrete sense, where a mixture literally stands together.
branches.cn: 物质质地：最古老的具体义，混合物在字面意义上“站在一起”。

intro.en: Consistency is built with -ency, a noun-of-state suffix, on the verb consist. The same base also takes -ent (consistent) and -ence (consistence), so the family shows how one Latin verb branches into several word classes.
intro.cn: consistency 由状态名词后缀 -ency 加在动词 consist 上构成。同一词基还接 -ent（consistent）和 -ence（consistence），因此这个词族展示了一个拉丁动词如何分成多个词类。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is consistere, from con- 'together' + sistere 'to stand'. Latin -entia gave the noun suffix; the English branch also uses -ent and -ence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 consistere，来自 con-“一起” + sistere“站立”。拉丁语 -entia 提供了名词后缀；英语这一支还使用 -ent 与 -ence。

items.meaning: to be composed of; to stand together
items.meaningCN: 由……组成；站在一起（con- 表示“一起”）
items.example: The team consists of five members.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队由五名成员组成。

items.meaning: always behaving or happening in the same way
items.meaningCN: 一致的；始终如一的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: Her story was consistent with the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 她的说法与证据一致。

items.meaning: in the same way every time
items.meaningCN: 一贯地（形容词 + -ly 构成副词）
items.example: He has consistently supported the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他一直支持这个计划。

items.meaning: the state of parts standing together
items.meaningCN: 一致性；连贯性（-ency 构成状态名词）
items.example: The consistency of the data surprised the researchers.
items.exampleCN: 数据的一致性让研究人员感到惊讶。

items.meaning: not staying the same; contradictory
items.meaningCN: 不一致的；矛盾的（in- 否定）
items.example: His accounts of the trip were inconsistent.
items.exampleCN: 他对这次旅行的叙述前后矛盾。

items.meaning: a case or quality of not agreeing
items.meaningCN: 不一致；矛盾之处（in- + -ency 名词）
items.example: The audit found several inconsistencies in the records.
items.exampleCN: 审计发现记录中有几处不一致。

items.meaning: an older form of consistency, especially of texture
items.meaningCN: consistency 的旧形式，尤指质地（-ence 变体）
items.example: The mixture had the consistence of honey.
items.exampleCN: 这混合物具有蜂蜜般的稠度。

items.meaning: the quality of not contradicting oneself
items.meaningCN: 自洽；自身一致（self- 表示“自我”）
items.example: The theory was praised for its self-consistency.
items.exampleCN: 该理论因自洽而受到称赞。

items.meaning: being made up of, used in the phrase 'consisting of'
items.meaningCN: 由……组成的（-ing 分词，用于 consisting of）
items.example: The committee, consisting of seven experts, met on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 由七名专家组成的委员会在周一开会。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand firm, take one's stand; to be composed of
to stand, stand still, set up

latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态或性质（构成抽象名词）

definition_zh: 一贯地；始终如一地；持续稳定地
definition_en: in a way that stays the same over time and does not change from one case to another
core_image: 节拍器以完全相同的间隔敲击，一次也不快、一次也不慢
scene: The lab technician consistently records the temperature at the same hour every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 consistently 是「一贯地、始终如一地」（第 1 个义项：以同样的方式反复做）；句意：实验室技术员每天早上都在同一时间记录温度，从不间断。图中可辨识物件：温度计、记录本、挂钟、实验台。

pos.zh: 一贯地；始终如一地；持续稳定地

senses.title: In the same way every time
senses.titleCN: 一贯地：每次都一样
senses.definition: in a way that does not change from one occasion to the next
senses.definitionCN: 以不随场合改变的方式
senses.example: The lab technician consistently records the temperature at the same hour every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室技术员每天早上都在同一时间记录温度。
senses.why: Consistently is consistent + -ly. Consistent comes from the present-participle stem of consist, from Latin consistere 'stand firm'. An action done consistently is an action that keeps standing in the same place, occasion after occasion.
senses.whyCN: consistently 是 consistent + -ly。consistent 来自 consist 的现在分词词干，而 consist 出自拉丁语 consistere“站稳”。一贯地做一件事，就是让这个动作在一次次场合中始终站在同一个位置。

senses.title: Consistently high: keeping a high level
senses.titleCN: 持续保持高水平：长期维持高位
senses.definition: remaining at a high level over a period, without falling
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内保持高水平而不下降
senses.example: The school has consistently high graduation rates.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的毕业率持续保持在高位。
senses.why: The -ly adverb measures how an adjective holds over time. A consistently high level is one that stands firm at the top instead of rising and falling; the 'standing' image is applied to a position on a scale.
senses.whyCN: -ly 副词衡量一个形容词状态在时间中如何维持。持续偏高的水平，就是稳稳站在高位而不上下起伏；“站立”的形象被用到了刻度上的位置。

senses.title: Consistently apply: use the same rule everywhere
senses.titleCN: 一致适用：到处使用同一规则
senses.definition: to apply a rule, standard, or method in the same way to every case
senses.definitionCN: 把规则、标准或方法以相同方式用于每个情形
senses.example: The referee consistently applied the new rule throughout the season.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在整个赛季一致适用新规则。
senses.why: Consistent originally meant 'standing together'. When a rule is applied, the cases must all stand together under one standard. The -ly adverb says the standard is not bent from case to case.
senses.whyCN: consistent 原意是“站在一起”。适用规则时，所有情形都必须站在同一标准之下。-ly 副词说明这个标准不会因情形不同而弯曲。

senses.title: Perform consistently: deliver a steady standard
senses.titleCN: 稳定表现：交付稳定水准
senses.definition: to perform at a steady level without large swings in quality
senses.definitionCN: 以稳定水平表现，质量没有大幅波动
senses.example: She performs consistently well under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下表现始终稳定。
senses.why: Performance varies across events, and consistency is what makes those events 'stand together'. The adverb marks the absence of swings: each showing holds the same level as the last.
senses.whyCN: 表现会随场次变化，而 consistency 就是让这些场次“站在一起”的东西。这个副词标记的正是没有波动：每一次表现都与上一次保持同一水平。

senses.title: Consistently follow: keep obeying a rule
senses.titleCN: 始终遵循：一直遵从
senses.definition: to keep following a rule, instruction, or procedure without exception
senses.definitionCN: 无例外地一直遵照规则、指示或程序
senses.example: All staff have consistently followed the safety procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工始终遵循安全程序。
senses.why: Following is a repeated act, and -ly says the repetition never breaks. The base image of standing firm becomes temporal: the behaviour stays in line instead of drifting away.
senses.whyCN: 遵循是反复发生的动作，-ly 说明这种重复从未中断。“站稳”的词基形象在此变成时间性的：行为始终留在线上，而不是漂走。

senses.title: Consistently accurate: keeping the same precision
senses.titleCN: 始终保持准确：精度一直不变
senses.definition: remaining accurate to the same degree on every occasion
senses.definitionCN: 每次都以相同程度保持准确
senses.example: The old scale has remained consistently accurate for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧秤十年来始终保持准确。
senses.why: Accuracy can drift; consistently says it does not. The suffix -ly converts 'standing firm' into a manner of measurement: the readings keep standing at the true value.
senses.whyCN: 准确度会漂移；consistently 说明它没有漂。后缀 -ly 把“站稳”转成一种测量方式：读数一直站在真值上。

senses.title: Consistently better: always ahead in comparison
senses.titleCN: 一直更好：比较中始终领先
senses.definition: better than the alternative on every or almost every occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在每次或几乎每次场合都比另一选择更好
senses.example: Their new model has consistently outperformed the older one.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的新模型一直比旧模型表现更好。
senses.why: With a comparative, -ly says the comparison keeps the same result. The gap may be small, but it never reverses; that is 'standing firm' applied to a ranking.
senses.whyCN: 与比较级连用时，-ly 说明比较结果始终不变。差距也许不大，但从不反转；这就是“站稳”用在排名上。

senses.title: Consistently support: back something at every turn
senses.titleCN: 始终支持：每次都站在同一边
senses.definition: to support a person, plan, or policy on every relevant occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在每个相关场合都支持某人、某计划或某政策
senses.example: The mayor has consistently supported the housing project.
senses.exampleCN: 市长始终支持这个住房项目。
senses.why: Support is a stance, and a stance can be held. Consistently turns that stance into a long-held position: the person keeps standing on the same side of the question.
senses.whyCN: 支持是一种立场，而立场可以被“守住”。consistently 把这种立场变成长期保持的位置：此人在问题上始终站在同一边。

senses.title: Consistently refuse: say no every time
senses.titleCN: 一贯拒绝：每次都说不
senses.definition: to refuse something every time it is proposed or offered
senses.definitionCN: 每当某事被提出或提供时都拒绝
senses.example: The committee has consistently refused to release the minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会一贯拒绝公布会议记录。
senses.why: Refusal can be a one-off act; consistently makes it a settled policy. The adverb adds the same temporal firmness: the answer stands firm each time the question returns.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝可以是一次性动作；consistently 把它变成既定政策。副词增添了同样的时间性坚定：每当问题再次出现，答案都稳稳不变。

intro.en: Consistently is consistent + -ly, where consistent itself comes from consist plus -ent. The chain is Latin consistere 'stand firm' → English consist → consistent → consistently. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consistently 是 consistent + -ly，而 consistent 本身来自 consist 加 -ent。链条是拉丁语 consistere“站稳” → 英语 consist → consistent → consistently。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Latin consistere means 'to take one's stand, stand firm; to be composed of'. It is con- 'together' + sistere 'to stand'. The physical image is a group of things holding a position together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consistere 意为“站定、站稳；由……构成”。它是 con-“一起” + sistere“站立”。具体形象是若干事物一起守住一个位置。

items.en: English consist is borrowed from consistere. Its early sense 'to have a settled position' yields the modern 'to be made up of', which is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: 英语 consist 借自 consistere。早期“占据稳定位置”的义项发展出现代“由……构成”，后者成为整个词族的基础。

items.en: Consist's present-participle stem consistent- plus -ent (Latin -ent-, adjective suffix) gives consistent: literally 'standing firm, holding together'. The suffix makes a quality adjective out of the verb's action.
items.cn: consist 的现在分词词干 consistent- 加 -ent（拉丁语 -ent-，形容词后缀）构成 consistent：字面是“站稳的、保持在一起的”。后缀把动词动作变成性质形容词。

items.en: Consistent + -ly (Old English -lice) forms consistently, 'in a consistent manner'. This is the key step of this entry: the adjective's stable quality becomes the manner of an action.
items.cn: consistent + -ly（古英语 -lice）构成 consistently，意为“以一致的方式”。这是本条目的关键一步：形容词的稳定性质变成了动作的方式。

items.en: The literal 'standing firm' first described physical position, then character, then repeated behaviour. With -ly the emphasis moves to time: the same standard is held across many occasions, not just at one moment.
items.cn: 字面的“站稳”先描述物理位置，再描述性格，最后描述重复行为。加 -ly 后重心转向时间：同一标准在众多场合中被保持，而不只维持于一瞬。

items.en: Modern English uses consistently with verbs of performance, application, support and refusal, and with comparatives such as 'consistently better'. The word has become a general marker of reliable repetition.
items.cn: 现代英语把 consistently 用于表现、适用、支持、拒绝等动词，也用于 consistently better 这类比较级。这个词已成为“可靠重复”的通用标记。

note.en: The first group lists close spellings and family forms; the second lists adverbs with a similar meaning.
note.cn: 第一组列出拼写相近及同族形式；第二组列出意思相近的副词。

entries.definition: always behaving or happening in the same way. It is the adjective behind consistently.
entries.definitionCN: 始终以相同方式行事或发生的。它是 consistently 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: to be made up of particular parts. It is the root verb of the family, not an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定部分构成。它是这个词族的根动词，不是副词。

entries.definition: in a forceful, demanding way. It comes from insist, a different prefix and a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 以强硬、要求的方式。它来自 insist，前缀不同，意思也不同。

entries.definition: at fixed intervals or on a habitual basis. It stresses timing rather than sameness of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔或习惯性地。它强调时间规律，而不是品质相同。

entries.definition: in the same way in every case. It is closer to 'identically' than consistently is.
entries.definitionCN: 在每种情况下都以相同方式。它比 consistently 更接近“完全相同地”。

entries.definition: in a continuous, even way. It often describes gradual change or pace.
entries.definitionCN: 以连续、平稳的方式。它常描述逐渐变化或节奏。

entries.definition: in a way that can be trusted to happen or work. It stresses dependability rather than sameness.
entries.definitionCN: 以可被信赖会发生或奏效的方式。它强调可靠，而不是相同。

entries.definition: always, with no exception. It is stronger and more absolute than consistently.
entries.definitionCN: 总是，没有例外。它比 consistently 更强、更绝对。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real consist family, the real -ent and -ly chain, and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 consist 词族、真实的 -ent 与 -ly 链条，以及真实搭配。

normal.en: consist means 'stand together'; consistent means 'standing together'; consistently means 'in a standing-together way'. The family keeps one picture.
normal.cn: consist 意为“站在一起”；consistent 意为“站得住的”；consistently 意为“以站得住的方式”。整个词族保持同一个画面。

normal.en: consist → consistent → consistently is a clean three-step ladder: verb, adjective, adverb.
normal.cn: consist → consistent → consistently 是一架清晰的三级梯子：动词、形容词、副词。

normal.en: The common frames are consistently high, consistently perform, consistently apply, consistently support, consistently refuse.
normal.cn: 常见框架有 consistently high、consistently perform、consistently apply、consistently support、consistently refuse。

normal.en: Do not confuse consistent with constant: constant means 'never stopping', consistent means 'not changing shape from case to case'.
normal.cn: 不要把 consistent 与 constant 混淆：constant 是“从不停歇”，consistent 是“在不同情形下不变形”。

normal.en: With comparatives, consistently means 'every time, not just once': consistently better, consistently ahead.
normal.cn: 与比较级连用时，consistently 表示“每次都如此，而不只一次”：consistently better、consistently ahead。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome: its ticks are the repeated occasions, and consistently is the identical interval between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个节拍器：它的敲击就是一次次场合，而 consistently 就是它们之间完全相同的间隔。

abstract.en: The word is a line drawn through many points. Each point may differ, but the line does not bend.
abstract.cn: 这个词是穿过许多点的一条线。每个点可以不同，但线本身不弯。

abstract.en: All nine senses keep one promise: what happened last time will happen again in the same way.
abstract.cn: 九个义项都信守同一个承诺：上次怎样发生，这次还以同样的方式发生。

examples.en: The team has consistently delivered high-quality work.
examples.cn: 这个团队一直交付高质量的工作。

examples.en: The same rules must be consistently applied to every applicant.
examples.cn: 同样的规则必须一致适用于每位申请者。

examples.en: She has consistently refused to discuss the matter.
examples.cn: 她一贯拒绝讨论此事。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯细思坦特利”——肯细细思量，站得稳、做得利落 → consistently 一贯地

root: consist（拉丁 consistere“站稳、站在一起”）+ -ent（形容词后缀）+ -ly（副词后缀）：以始终站得住、不改变的方式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of consistently all describe repetition without drift. The repeated thing may be a level, a rule, a performance, a reading, a comparison, a stance, or a refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: consistently 的九个义项都描述“重复而不漂移”。重复的对象可以是水平、规则、表现、读数、比较、立场或拒绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metronome ticking at exactly the same interval.
core.cn: 核心意象：节拍器以完全相同的间隔敲击。

branches.en: GENERAL HABIT AND OBEDIENCE: doing or following the same thing each time.
branches.cn: 一般习惯与遵从：每次都做或遵循同一件事。

branches.en: LEVEL AND PERFORMANCE: keeping a high or steady standard across events.
branches.cn: 水平与表现：在各次事件中保持高而稳的水准。

branches.en: RULES AND ACCURACY: applying one standard everywhere, and holding the same precision.
branches.cn: 规则与准确：到处适用同一标准，并保持同样的精度。

branches.en: COMPARISON AND REFUSAL: always ahead in a ranking, or always saying no.
branches.cn: 比较与拒绝：在排名中始终领先，或始终说不。

branches.en: POLITICAL STANCE: supporting the same side at every turn.
branches.cn: 立场：在每个场合都支持同一边。

intro.en: Consistently is the end of a three-stage suffix chain: -ent turns the verb consist into the adjective consistent, and -ly turns that adjective into an adverb of manner. No prefix is involved.
intro.cn: consistently 是三级后缀链条的末端：-ent 把动词 consist 变成形容词 consistent，-ly 再把形容词变成方式副词。这里不涉及前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is consistere 'stand firm', built from con- 'together' + sistere 'to stand'. Latin supplies the base and -ent; -ly is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 consistere“站稳”，由 con-“一起” + sistere“站立”构成。拉丁语提供词基和 -ent；-ly 是英语本族后缀。

items.meaning: to be composed of; to stand together
items.meaningCN: 由……组成；站在一起
items.example: The cake consists of flour, eggs, and sugar.
items.exampleCN: 这个蛋糕由面粉、鸡蛋和糖组成。

items.meaning: staying the same; holding together
items.meaningCN: 一致的；始终如一的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: His results have been consistent all year.
items.exampleCN: 他全年的成绩一直很稳定。

items.meaning: in the same way every time
items.meaningCN: 一贯地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The machine runs consistently at full speed.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器一直全速稳定运转。

items.meaning: the state of standing together
items.meaningCN: 一致性；连贯性（-ency 构成名词）
items.example: Consistency is more important than speed.
items.exampleCN: 一致性比速度更重要。

items.meaning: not staying the same; contradictory
items.meaningCN: 不一致的；矛盾的（in- 否定）
items.example: The two reports are inconsistent.
items.exampleCN: 这两份报告不一致。

items.meaning: in a way that keeps changing
items.meaningCN: 不一致地；时好时坏地
items.example: The rules were applied inconsistently.
items.exampleCN: 规则适用得并不一致。

items.meaning: was made up of (past tense)
items.meaningCN: 由……组成（过去式／过去分词）
items.example: The original team consisted of three people.
items.exampleCN: 最初的团队由三个人组成。

items.meaning: being made up of
items.meaningCN: 由……组成的（现在分词）
items.example: A team consisting of six players won the match.
items.exampleCN: 一支由六名队员组成的队伍赢得了比赛。

items.meaning: not contradicting itself
items.meaningCN: 自洽的；自身一致的（self- 表示“自我”）
items.example: The model is mathematically self-consistent.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型在数学上是自洽的。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand firm; to be composed of

latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示具有某种性质的（形容词后缀）

definition_en: one of the parts that together make up a whole; a voter in a district; as an adjective, forming or helping to establish something
core_image: 一块块砖被砌进同一面墙：每块砖都是墙的组成部分

sceneCN: 这里 constituent 是「制宪的」（第 3 个义项：制宪会议）；句意：在制宪会议上，代表们争论新国家应当如何建立。图中可辨识物件：会议长桌、国旗草案、代表证、投票箱。

senses.title: A part that makes up a whole
senses.titleCN: 组成部分：构成整体的一部分
senses.definition: one of the separate parts that together form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 共同构成一个整体的各个部分之一
senses.example: Each constituent of the machine can be replaced separately.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器的每个组成部分都可以单独更换。
senses.why: Constituent comes from Latin constituens, the present participle of constituere 'to set up, establish'. A constituent is literally 'a thing set into' a larger whole: it has been placed in the structure and helps hold it up.
senses.whyCN: constituent 来自拉丁语 constituens，即 constituere“设立、建立”的现在分词。组成部分字面上就是“被安置进”更大整体中的东西：它被放进结构里，并帮助撑起结构。

senses.title: A substance that forms part of a mixture
senses.titleCN: 物质成分：混合物中的某种成分
senses.definition: a substance that is one of the materials making up a mixture or structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成混合物或结构的一种材料
senses.example: Calcium is a key constituent of bone.
senses.exampleCN: 钙是骨骼的一种关键成分。
senses.why: The same 'set into' image applies to matter: a chemical constituent has been placed into the mixture and is part of its make-up. The -ent form names the thing that has been constituted into the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“被安置进去”的形象也适用于物质：化学成分被放进混合物，成为其组成的一部分。-ent 形式命名那个被构成进整体的东西。

senses.title: Constituent assembly: a body that sets up a state
senses.titleCN: 制宪会议：设立国家的机构
senses.definition: a specially elected assembly whose task is to draw up a constitution
senses.definitionCN: 为起草宪法而专门选出的代表会议
senses.example: The constituent assembly drafted the new republic's charter.
senses.exampleCN: 制宪会议起草了新共和国的宪章。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the verb's active force: a constituent assembly is an assembly that constitutes, that sets up the state's fundamental order. Here the word describes the setting-up act itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了动词的主动力量：constituent assembly 就是“进行构成”的会议，它设立国家的基本秩序。这里这个词描述的是“设立”这一行为本身。

senses.title: Constituent country: a unit inside a union
senses.titleCN: 构成国：联合体内的组成单位
senses.definition: a country or state that forms part of a larger political union, such as the United Kingdom
senses.definitionCN: 构成更大政治联合体（如英国）的一部分的国家或地区
senses.example: Scotland is a constituent country of the United Kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰是英国的构成国。
senses.why: A constituent country is a country that helps constitute a larger state. The same participle logic applies: it is a unit set into the union. Note that the voting district itself is a constituency, not a constituent.
senses.whyCN: 构成国是帮助构成更大国家的国家。同样的分词逻辑：它是被安置进联合体的单位。注意：选区本身是 constituency，而不是 constituent。

senses.title: A grammatical unit in a sentence
senses.titleCN: 语法成分：句子中的结构单位
senses.definition: a word or group of words that functions as a single unit within a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在句子中作为一个单位起作用的词或词组
senses.example: In 'the old bridge', the whole phrase is a constituent of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 在 the old bridge 中，整个短语是句子的一个成分。
senses.why: Modern linguistics borrowed the word for structure: a constituent is a piece 'set into' a larger sentence and can be moved or replaced as a unit. The Latin 'standing in a structure' sense becomes grammatical analysis.
senses.whyCN: 现代语言学借这个词来描述结构：语法成分是“被安置进”更大句子的片段，可以作为一个单位移动或替换。拉丁语“站在结构中”的意思变成了语法分析。

senses.title: An essential element of a concept or situation
senses.titleCN: 构成要素：使事物成立的关键元素
senses.definition: an element that is necessary for something to exist or be what it is
senses.definitionCN: 某事物存在或成为自身所必需的元素
senses.example: Trust is a constituent element of a healthy partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是健康合作关系的一个构成要素。
senses.why: The word moves from physical parts to abstract ones. A constituent element is still something 'set into' the whole, but now the whole is a relationship or idea rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物质部分转向抽象部分。构成要素仍然是“被安置进”整体的东西，只是这个整体现在是关系或观念，而不是物体。

senses.title: A voter in a district
senses.titleCN: 选民：选区中有投票权的人
senses.definition: a person who lives in an electoral district and has the right to vote there
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一选区并有投票权的人
senses.example: The senator met with constituents at the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 参议员在市政厅会见选民。
senses.why: In political usage the person 'constitutes' the electorate: voters set up the representative body. The noun shifted from 'one who constitutes' to 'one who is represented', a concrete political role.
senses.whyCN: 在政治用法中，个人“构成”选民群体：选民设立了代议机构。名词从“构成者”转为“被代表者”，成为一个具体的政治角色。

senses.title: Constituent power: the authority to found a state
senses.titleCN: 制宪权：创立国家的权力
senses.definition: the ultimate authority of a people to establish or change its constitution
senses.definitionCN: 人民设立或改变其宪法的终极权力
senses.example: The court debated whether the people hold constituent power.
senses.exampleCN: 法院讨论了人民是否拥有制宪权。
senses.why: Here the adjective names the power that constitutes: the capacity to set up the legal order itself. It is the most abstract extension of constituere 'establish', applied to the founding act rather than to a part.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词命名“进行构成”的权力：设立法律秩序本身的能力。这是 constituere“建立”最抽象的延伸，作用于创立行为而非某个部分。

senses.title: Constituent structure: the arrangement of parts
senses.titleCN: 成分结构：各部分的层级组织
senses.definition: the hierarchical arrangement of parts within a sentence or system
senses.definitionCN: 句子或系统内部各部分的层级排列方式
senses.example: The tree diagram shows the constituent structure of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 树形图展示了这个句子的成分结构。
senses.why: Structure names the way constituents are set together. The word keeps its compositional sense but now describes the whole arrangement rather than any single part; -ent still marks the unit that has been set in.
senses.whyCN: 结构命名各成分被放在一起的方式。这个词保留组合义，但现在描述整体排列而非单个部分；-ent 仍标记那个被安置进去的单位。

intro.en: Constituent is a Latin present participle in -ent, from constituere 'set up, establish'. The base verb splits into con- 'together' + statuere 'place, set'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: constituent 是带 -ent 的拉丁语现在分词，来自 constituere“设立、建立”。基础动词拆为 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Constituere means 'to set up, establish, appoint, constitute'. It is a compound of con- 'together' and statuere 'to place, set, fix'.
items.cn: constituere 意为“设立、建立、任命、构成”。它由 con-“一起”和 statuere“放置、设立、固定”复合而成。

items.en: Its present participle is constituens, stem constituent-, 'setting up; that which sets up'. This is the exact form English borrows, so the word arrives already carrying the active idea of putting something in place.
items.cn: 它的现在分词是 constituens，词干 constituent-，意为“正在设立的；设立者”。英语借用的正是这一形式，因此这个词一进入英语就带着“把某物安放到位”的主动含义。

items.en: The -ent suffix (Latin -ent-) makes an adjective or noun from the participle. As an adjective, constituent means 'forming part of'; as a noun, 'the thing that constitutes' or 'one who constitutes'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ent（拉丁语 -ent-）把分词变成形容词或名词。作形容词时 constituent 意为“构成部分的”；作名词时意为“构成之物”或“构成者”。

items.en: English adopts constituent in the 16c. as both adjective and noun, first in the general sense 'forming part of a whole'. The political senses grow from the idea of parts that set up a larger body.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪引入 constituent，形容词与名词并用，最初是一般义“构成整体的一部分”。政治义从“设立更大机构的部分”这一观念生长出来。

items.en: By the 18c. a constituent is 'a person who has the right to elect a representative'. The voter is the person who constitutes the representative body, so the noun moves from maker to member of the electorate.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，constituent 指“有权选举代表的人”。选民是构成代议机构的人，因此名词从“构成者”转为“选民群体的一员”。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense (a constituent of a mixture), the political senses (constituent assembly, constituent power, voter), and the 20c. linguistic sense of a syntactic unit.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物质义（混合物的成分）、政治义（制宪会议、制宪权、选民），以及 20 世纪语言学的句法单位义。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that are often confused with constituent; the second holds nouns that also name a part of a whole.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 constituent 混淆的同族词；第二组是同样表示“整体的一部分”的名词。

entries.definition: a voting district or the voters in it. It is the place or group, while a constituent is one voter.
entries.definitionCN: 选区或该区选民。它是地区或群体，而 constituent 是其中一位选民。

entries.definition: to form or make up something; to establish. It is the verb behind constituent.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物；设立。它是 constituent 背后的动词。

entries.definition: the fundamental law of a state, or the make-up of a body. It is the -tion noun from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 国家的根本法，或身体的构成。它是同一动词加 -tion 的名词。

entries.definition: a part of a larger machine or system. It is close to constituent but more common in technical contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 较大机器或系统的一部分。它与 constituent 接近，但更常用于技术语境。

entries.definition: one of the basic parts of something. It is broader and can be abstract or chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的基本部分之一。它更宽泛，可指抽象要素或化学元素。

entries.definition: one of the foods or substances combined to make something. It is mostly used for cooking and mixtures.
entries.definitionCN: 组合成某物的食材或物质之一。它多用于烹饪和混合物。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. It is the everyday word that constituent formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分。它是 constituent 所正式化的日常词。

entries.definition: one element that contributes to a result. It is about influence rather than physical make-up.
entries.definitionCN: 促成结果的一个要素。它讲的是影响，而不是物理构成。

normalIntro.en: These links use the real constituere family, the real -ent participle ending, and real political collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联系使用真实的 constituere 词族、真实的分词后缀 -ent，以及真实政治搭配。

normal.en: con- 'together' + statuere 'set' + -ent 'the one doing': a constituent is a thing set into the whole.
normal.cn: con-“一起” + statuere“放置” + -ent“做此事者”：constituent 就是被安置进整体的东西。

normal.en: Keep the family apart: constitute is the verb, constituent is a part or voter, constitution is the fundamental law, constituency is the district.
normal.cn: 分清词族：constitute 是动词，constituent 是部分或选民，constitution 是根本法，constituency 是选区。

normal.en: The political phrases are fixed: constituent assembly, constituent power, constituent country.
normal.cn: 政治短语是固定的：constituent assembly、constituent power、constituent country。

normal.en: A constituent is one voter; all the voters together form a constituency. One letter changes the unit.
normal.cn: 一位选民是 constituent；全体选民构成 constituency。一个字母之差，单位就变了。

normal.en: In grammar, a constituent is any word or phrase that can stand as a unit inside a larger sentence.
normal.cn: 在语法中，成分是任何能在更大句子中作为一个单位站立的词或短语。

abstract.en: Picture a wall: each brick is set into it and helps hold it up. That brick is a constituent; the wall is the whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙：每块砖都被砌进去，并帮助撑住墙。那块砖就是 constituent，墙则是整体。

abstract.en: The word always implies placement. A constituent is not just nearby; it has been put in and is part of the structure.
abstract.cn: 这个词总含有“被安放”的意味。组成部分不是仅仅在旁边，而是被放进去、成为结构的一部分。

abstract.en: The voter sense keeps the same logic: voters are the pieces that set up the representative body.
abstract.cn: 选民义保留同一逻辑：选民是设立代议机构的那些“部件”。

examples.en: Protein is a major constituent of every living cell.
examples.cn: 蛋白质是每个活细胞的主要成分。

examples.en: The constituent assembly began drafting the constitution in 1787.
examples.cn: 制宪会议于 1787 年开始起草宪法。

examples.en: The representative holds a weekly meeting with her constituents.
examples.cn: 这位代表每周与她的选民会面。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯斯提球恩特”——肯斯提把球摁特进墙里，每块砖都是组成部分 → constituent 成分

root: 拉丁 constituere“设立、放置”（con- 一起 + statuere 放置）+ -ent（分词后缀）：被安置进整体、构成本身的那一部分。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of constituent all come from 'something set into a whole'. The whole may be a machine, a mixture, a state, a sentence, a relationship, or an electorate.
sensesIntro.cn: constituent 的九个义项都来自“被安置进整体的东西”。这个整体可以是机器、混合物、国家、句子、关系或选民群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brick set into a wall, each brick helping to hold the wall up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块块砖被砌进同一面墙，每块砖都帮助撑住墙。

branches.en: PART AND ELEMENT: a concrete part of a whole, and an essential element of an idea or situation.
branches.cn: 部分与要素：整体的具体部分，以及观念或情境中不可缺少的元素。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND STRUCTURE: a substance inside a mixture, and the arrangement of all the parts.
branches.cn: 物质与结构：混合物中的物质成分，以及所有部分的排列方式。

branches.en: FOUNDING: an assembly that sets up a state, and the ultimate power to do so.
branches.cn: 创立：设立国家的会议，以及这样做的终极权力。

branches.en: POLITICAL MEMBERSHIP: a unit inside a union, and a voter inside a district.
branches.cn: 政治成员：联合体内部的组成单位，以及选区内部的选民。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word or phrase functioning as one structural unit.
branches.cn: 语法：作为一个结构单位起作用的词或短语。

intro.en: Constituent is built from the Latin participle constituens. English adds no new prefix here; the -ent ending is the same suffix that makes adjectives such as consistent and different.
intro.cn: constituent 由拉丁语分词 constituens 构成。英语在这里没有再加新前缀；-ent 就是构成 consistent、different 等形容词的同一个后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is constituere, from con- 'together' + statuere 'place, set'. Constituens is its present participle, and the -ent- stem is what English borrows.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 constituere，来自 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。constituens 是它的现在分词，英语借用的就是 -ent- 词干。

items.meaning: to form, make up, or establish
items.meaningCN: 构成；设立（con- 表示“一起”）
items.example: Twelve members constitute the committee.
items.exampleCN: 十二名成员构成了这个委员会。

items.meaning: a part that makes up a whole
items.meaningCN: 组成部分；成分（-ent 分词后缀）
items.example: Water is a constituent of every cell.
items.exampleCN: 水是每个细胞的成分。

items.meaning: the fundamental law or make-up of something
items.meaningCN: 宪法；体质；构成（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The country adopted a new constitution.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家通过了新宪法。

items.meaning: relating to a constitution
items.meaningCN: 宪法的；合宪的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The court reviewed the constitutional question.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了这个宪法问题。

items.meaning: a voting district or its voters
items.meaningCN: 选区；选民群体（-cy 构成名词）
items.example: The candidate visited every town in the constituency.
items.exampleCN: 候选人走访了选区的每个城镇。

items.meaning: more than one part or voter
items.meaningCN: 多个组成部分或选民（复数后缀）
items.example: The medicine contains several active constituents.
items.exampleCN: 这种药含有几种活性成分。

items.meaning: formed or established in the past
items.meaningCN: 构成了；设立了（过去式／过去分词）
items.example: The tribunal was constituted in 1998.

items.meaning: forming or making up

items.example: The fields constituting the park are protected.

items.meaning: essential to the make-up of something

items.example: Language is a constitutive part of human culture.
items.exampleCN: 语言是人类文化的构成性部分。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示具有某种性质或执行某动作的

definition_en: the fundamental laws of a state; the physical make-up of a person or thing; a set of rules for an organization

senses.title: The fundamental law of a state
senses.titleCN: 根本法：国家的宪法
senses.definition: the set of basic laws and principles by which a state is governed
senses.definitionCN: 治理国家所依据的基本法律与原则
senses.example: The constitution guarantees freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法保障言论自由。
senses.why: Constitution comes from Latin constitutio, 'a setting up, an ordinance', from constituere 'set up'. The constitution is the document that sets up the state's legal order: it is the founding structure, not one law among many.
senses.whyCN: constitution 来自拉丁语 constitutio“设立、法规”，源自 constituere“设立”。宪法就是设立国家法律秩序的文件：它是地基性的结构，而不是众多法律中的一条。

senses.title: The Constitution: the US founding document
senses.titleCN: 美国宪法：首字母大写的建国文件
senses.definition: the Constitution, especially the written founding document of the United States
senses.definitionCN: 特指美国成文建国文件《美国宪法》
senses.example: The Constitution was signed in Philadelphia in 1787.
senses.exampleCN: 《美国宪法》于 1787 年在费城签署。
senses.why: A capitalized proper noun narrows the general word to one specific founding document. The name keeps the literal sense 'that which sets up': the text constitutes the federal government and divides its powers.
senses.whyCN: 首字母大写把普通名词缩小为一份特定的建国文件。这个名称保留字面义“设立之物”：这部文本构成了联邦政府并划分其权力。

senses.title: A person's physical condition
senses.titleCN: 体质：人的身体状况
senses.definition: a person's general physical strength, health, or ability to resist illness
senses.definitionCN: 一个人总体的体力、健康状况或抗病能力
senses.example: He has a strong constitution and rarely catches colds.
senses.exampleCN: 他体质强壮，很少感冒。
senses.why: The same word for the state's frame applies to the body's frame. Latin constitutio could already mean 'composition, make-up'; how a body is 'set up' is its constitution.
senses.whyCN: 用来指国家框架的同一个词，也用来指身体框架。拉丁语 constitutio 本就可指“组成、构造”；身体被“设立”的方式，就是体质。

senses.title: The rules of an organization
senses.titleCN: 组织章程：团体的规则
senses.definition: the set of rules by which a club, company, or other organization is governed
senses.definitionCN: 管理俱乐部、公司或其他组织的规则集
senses.example: The committee wrote the club's constitution before electing its first president.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在选出第一任主席之前先写好了俱乐部的章程。
senses.why: The 'setting up' sense scales down: a club also needs a founding document that establishes its offices and procedures. The constitution is the small state's frame of government.
senses.whyCN: “设立”义可以缩小尺度：俱乐部也需要一份设立其职位与程序的建章文件。章程就是这个小共同体的治理框架。

senses.title: The make-up of a substance
senses.titleCN: 物质构成：某物的组成方式
senses.definition: the way in which something is composed or made up
senses.definitionCN: 某事物由哪些部分构成、如何构成
senses.example: The constitution of the soil affects what can grow there.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤的构成影响那里能种什么。
senses.why: Here the noun names the result of constituere 'to compose': the parts set together. It is close to 'composition', but constitution stresses the arrangement that makes the thing what it is.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词命名 constituere“组合”的结果：被放在一起的各部分。它接近 composition，但 constitution 更强调使该物成为自身的排列方式。

senses.title: A written constitution: the document itself
senses.titleCN: 成文宪法：宪法文件本身
senses.definition: a formal written document containing a state's fundamental rules
senses.definitionCN: 载有国家基本规则的正式书面文件
senses.example: Unlike Britain, the United States has a written constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 与美国不同，英国没有成文宪法。
senses.why: The word can shift from the legal order to the physical document that records it. 'Written' makes the document concrete, but the content is still the founding frame established by constituere.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从法律秩序转指记录它的实体文件。written 使文件具体化，但内容仍是由 constituere 设立的建国框架。

senses.title: A constitutional amendment
senses.titleCN: 宪法修正案：对宪法的正式修改
senses.definition: a formal change added to a constitution under its own amendment rules
senses.definitionCN: 依据宪法自身的修改规则所作出的正式变更
senses.example: The First Amendment to the Constitution protects freedom of assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 《宪法第一修正案》保护集会自由。
senses.why: An amendment is a later 'setting' added to the original frame. The word constitution still names the whole structure, while the amendment names one piece deliberately placed into it.
senses.whyCN: 修正案是后来加进原有框架的一条“设置”。constitution 仍命名整个结构，而 amendment 命名被有意放进去的一个部件。

senses.title: The build of a ship (technical)
senses.titleCN: 船只构造：船体结构（技术义）
senses.definition: the structural build or classification of a ship, especially in older technical usage
senses.definitionCN: 船只的结构构造或分级，尤见于较早的技术用法
senses.example: The old register recorded the constitution of each vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 旧登记册记录了每艘船的结构构造。
senses.why: This is the most concrete survival of 'how a thing is set up'. A ship's constitution is the way its hull and frames are put together; the sense is technical and now uncommon, but it follows the same compositional logic.
senses.whyCN: 这是“事物如何被设立”最具体的残留。船的 constitution 就是船体与骨架被组合起来的方式；这个义项偏技术、现已少见，但遵循同样的组合逻辑。

senses.title: The structure of the body
senses.titleCN: 身体构造：身体的组织结构
senses.definition: the anatomical arrangement and condition of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体在解剖上的排列与状态
senses.example: A runner's constitution determines how her joints handle stress.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步者的身体构造决定她的关节如何承受压力。
senses.why: The physical branch goes one level deeper than 'general health': here the focus is the arrangement of parts. Constitution still means 'the way something is set up', now applied to bones, joints, and tissues.
senses.whyCN: 这一身体义比“总体健康”更深一层：焦点在部分的排列。constitution 仍表示“某物被设立的方式”，这里用于骨骼、关节与组织。

intro.en: Constitution is the noun of action from Latin constituere 'set up, establish', formed with -tio. The path is constituere → constitutio → English constitution. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: constitution 是拉丁语 constituere“设立、建立”的动作名词，由 -tio 构成。路径是 constituere → constitutio → 英语 constitution。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Constituere means 'to set up, establish, appoint'. It combines con- 'together' with statuere 'to place, set, fix'. The base picture is putting pieces together into a standing structure.
items.cn: constituere 意为“设立、建立、任命”。它由 con-“一起”与 statuere“放置、设立、固定”组合而成。基础画面是把部件放在一起，形成一个立得住的结构。

items.en: Its past participle constitutus supplies the stem for constitutio(nem), 'a setting up, establishment; an ordinance, regulation'. The -tio suffix turns the act of setting up into a noun.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 constitutus 提供 constitutio(nem) 的词干，意为“设立、建立；法规、政令”。后缀 -tio 把“设立”这一动作变成名词。

items.en: Old French constitucion passes into English in the 14c. with the broad sense 'law, regulation, ordinance'. At this stage it can name any established rule, not only a state's founding law.
items.cn: 古法语 constitucion 在 14 世纪进入英语，广义为“法律、规则、政令”。在这个阶段，它可以指任何已设立的规则，而不只是国家的建国法。

items.en: Political and legal usage narrows the word to the fundamental law of a state. The 'setting up' sense becomes specific: the constitution is the act and document by which a political order is established.
items.cn: 政治与法律用法把词义收窄到国家的根本法。“设立”义变得具体：宪法是建立政治秩序的行为与文件。

items.en: Written constitutions and the American Constitution make the document sense central. In the same period the physical sense 'make-up, composition' continues, giving 'a strong constitution' and later 'the constitution of a ship'.
items.cn: 成文宪法与《美国宪法》使“文件”义成为核心。同一时期，物质义“构造、组成”继续存在，产生 a strong constitution，后来又有 the constitution of a ship。

items.en: Modern English uses constitution for the state's fundamental law, a written document, an organization's rules, a person's health, and the composition of a thing. -tion marks the noun throughout.
items.cn: 现代英语用 constitution 指国家根本法、成文文件、组织章程、人的体质以及事物的构成。贯穿始终的名词标记是 -tion。

note.en: The first group contains same-family words that are often mixed up; the second contains nouns with a related meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的同族词；第二组是意思相关的名词。

entries.definition: a part that makes up a whole, or a voter. It is the -ent participle form, not the -tion noun.
entries.definitionCN: 构成整体的部分，或选民。它是 -ent 分词形式，不是 -tion 名词。

entries.definition: a voting district or the voters in it. It is a place or group, not a constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 选区或该区选民。它是地区或群体，不是宪法。

entries.definition: relating to a constitution; also, relating to a person's physical condition. It is the adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 与宪法有关的；也指与个人体质有关的。它是形容词形式。

entries.definition: a formal document granting rights or setting up an organization. It is often more specific than constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 授予权利或设立组织的正式文件。它通常比 constitution 更具体。

entries.definition: a law passed by a legislature. It is one law, while a constitution is the framework above ordinary laws.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的法律。它是一条法律，而宪法是普通法律之上的框架。

entries.definition: the way something is composed. It is the everyday word for the physical sense of constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的组成方式。它是 constitution 物质义的日常用词。

entries.definition: the shape and strength of a person's body. It is more visible and athletic than constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形态与力量。它比 constitution 更强调可见的、运动性的体格。

entries.definition: the parts that make up something and how they are arranged. It overlaps with the material sense.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物的部分及其排列方式。它与物质义重叠。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real constituere family, the real -tion suffix, and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想使用真实的 constituere 词族、真实的 -tion 后缀和真实搭配。

normal.en: con- 'together' + statuere 'set' + -tion 'the act or result': constitution is the setting-up of a state, a body, or an organization.
normal.cn: con-“一起” + statuere“放置” + -tion“行为或结果”：constitution 就是国家、身体或组织的“设立”。

normal.en: The family: constitute (verb) → constitution (noun) → constitutional (adjective) → constitutionally (adverb).
normal.cn: 词族：constitute（动词）→ constitution（名词）→ constitutional（形容词）→ constitutionally（副词）。

normal.en: The two everyday collocations are 'amend the constitution' and 'a strong constitution'. One is political, one is physical.
normal.cn: 两个日常搭配是 amend the constitution 和 a strong constitution。一个属政治，一个属身体。

normal.en: Capitalize the word when it names the US document: the Constitution.
normal.cn: 当它指美国那份文件时，首字母大写：the Constitution。

normal.en: The organizational sense scales the state sense down: a club's constitution is its small-scale frame of government.
normal.cn: 组织义是国家义的缩小版：俱乐部章程就是它小规模的治理框架。

abstract.en: Picture a building's foundation and load-bearing frame: the constitution decides what can be built above it and how.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋建筑的地基与承重框架：宪法决定上面能建什么、怎么建。

abstract.en: The same frame image works for a body: a strong constitution is a body whose parts are set together well enough to resist stress.
abstract.cn: 同一个框架意象也适用于身体：强壮的体质就是各部分组合得足够好、能抵抗压力的身体。

abstract.en: Every sense answers one question: what is this thing set up out of, and by what rules does it hold together?
abstract.cn: 每个义项都回答同一个问题：这个东西由什么设立而成，又按什么规则保持在一起？

examples.en: The constitution sets out the powers of each branch of government.
examples.cn: 宪法规定了政府各部门的权力。

examples.en: Years of hard training had given her a strong constitution.
examples.cn: 多年的艰苦训练给了她强壮的体质。

examples.en: The club amended its constitution to allow younger members to vote.
examples.cn: 俱乐部修改了章程，允许更年轻的成员投票。

dict_mnemonic.text: “康斯提兔神”——康斯坦丁抱着兔神像宣读根本法 → constitution 宪法

root: 拉丁 constituere“设立、建立”（con- 一起 + statuere 放置）+ -tion（名词后缀）：把各部分设立起来的行为、结果与根本框架。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of constitution all name a frame that has been set up: a state's fundamental law, its written document, a body's build, an organization's rules, or a substance's make-up.
sensesIntro.cn: constitution 的九个义项都命名一个被设立起来的框架：国家的根本法、成文文件、身体构造、组织章程，或物质的组成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a building's foundation and load-bearing frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋建筑的地基与承重结构。

branches.en: THE STATE'S FRAME: the fundamental law, the US founding document, and the written text itself.
branches.cn: 国家框架：根本法、美国建国文件，以及成文文本本身。

branches.en: THE BODY'S FRAME: general physical strength, and the anatomical arrangement of parts.
branches.cn: 身体框架：总体体力，以及身体各部分在解剖上的排列。

branches.en: ORGANIZATIONAL FRAME: the rules that set up a club or company.
branches.cn: 组织框架：设立俱乐部或公司的规则。

branches.en: MATERIAL FRAME: how a substance is composed, and the technical build of a ship.
branches.cn: 物质框架：某物如何构成，以及船只的技术性构造。

branches.en: AMENDMENT: a later piece deliberately set into the founding frame.
branches.cn: 修正案：后来被有意安放进建国框架的一块部件。

intro.en: Constitution is the -tion noun from constitute. The suffix turns the act of setting something up into the act itself, its result, and the document or frame that results.
intro.cn: constitution 是 constitute 加 -tion 的名词。这个后缀把“设立某物”的动作转成行为本身、其结果，以及由此产生的文件或框架。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is constituere, from con- 'together' + statuere 'set, place'. Its noun constitutio supplies the -tion pattern; the same verb family also gives constituent and constitutional.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 constituere，来自 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。它的名词 constitutio 提供 -tion 模式；同一动词词族还产生 constituent 与 constitutional。

items.meaning: to form, make up, or establish
items.meaningCN: 构成；设立（con- 表示“一起”）
items.example: These four states constitute the region.
items.exampleCN: 这四个州构成了该地区。

items.meaning: the founding law or make-up of something
items.meaningCN: 宪法；体质；构成（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The constitution protects basic rights.
items.exampleCN: 宪法保护基本权利。

items.meaning: relating to a constitution
items.meaningCN: 宪法的；合宪的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The law raises a constitutional issue.
items.exampleCN: 这项法律引发了宪法问题。

items.meaning: in accordance with the constitution
items.meaningCN: 依照宪法地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The measure was constitutionally valid.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施在宪法上是有效的。

items.meaning: the quality of being allowed by the constitution
items.meaningCN: 合宪性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The court will rule on the law's constitutionality.
items.exampleCN: 法院将裁定该法律是否合宪。

items.meaning: a part of a whole; a voter
items.meaningCN: 组成部分；选民（-ent 分词后缀）
items.example: Each constituent of the alloy has a role.
items.exampleCN: 合金的每种成分都有作用。

items.meaning: a voting district
items.meaningCN: 选区（-cy 构成名词）
items.example: She represents a rural constituency.
items.exampleCN: 她代表一个乡村选区。

items.meaning: more than one constitution
items.meaningCN: 多部宪法（复数后缀）
items.example: The two countries adopted similar constitutions.
items.exampleCN: 这两个国家通过了相似的宪法。

items.meaning: formed or established in the past
items.meaningCN: 设立了；构成了（过去式／过去分词）
items.example: The assembly was constituted in 1787.
items.exampleCN: 该会议于 1787 年设立。

the act or result of doing something
